title: The origin of excited states of the $Λ$ baryon at the SU(3) point from Lattice QCD
summary:
In this work we determine the finite-volume lattice QCD spectrum at the flavor symmetric $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ point in the meson-baryon singlet and octet irreducible representations. We construct the appropriate interpolation operators and perform the calculation on ensembles in quite large volume ($L=48$). We find three below-threshold energy levels, with the singlet having lower energy and the two octets being non-degenerate at one sigma, which for these large volumes ($M_π L\approx 14.5$) strongly suggests a bound state close to that energy at each of the irreducible representations.
  We confront this finite-volume spectrum with the prediction from UCHPT through the Lüscher method finding qualitative agreement. Finally we perform a re-fit of UCHPT free parameters to the available (experimental and lattice) data including the energy levels calculated in this work. This allows us to follow the pole trajectories to the physical point, identifying the $Λ(1405)$ as a lower octet, and $Λ(1380)$ as a singlet bound state in the $\mathrm{SU(3)}$ limit. Furthermore, $Λ(1670)$ is identified on a qualitative level as the heavier octet bound state and its relation to three-body final states is discussed.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the finite-volume meson-baryon spectrum at the SU(3) flavor-symmetric point using large-volume lattice QCD (L=48, M_πL≈14.5), identifies three subthreshold energy levels—suggesting bound states in singlet and octet representations—and matches them to UCHPT via Lüscher’s method; a combined fit to lattice and experimental data locates Λ(1405) as the lower octet, Λ(1380) as the singlet, and Λ(1670) as the heavier octet bound state, with discussion of its coupling to three-body channels.
AI.motivation: To resolve the long-standing structure of the Λ(1405) resonance—whether it is a molecular meson-baryon bound state and how its multiplet partners behave in the SU(3) limit—by computing the finite-volume spectrum at exact SU(3) symmetry and connecting it rigorously to effective field theory (UCHPT) via the Lüscher formalism.
AI.method: Lattice QCD calculation at the SU(3)-symmetric point on large-volume ensembles (L=48, M_πL≈14.5); construction of meson-baryon interpolation operators transforming in SU(3) singlet and octet irreps; extraction of subthreshold finite-volume energy levels; application of the Lüscher method to map finite-volume energies to infinite-volume scattering amplitudes; global re-fit of UCHPT low-energy constants using both new lattice data and experimental observables; pole trajectory analysis toward the physical point.
AI.result: Three subthreshold energy levels found: one singlet (lowest) and two non-degenerate octets (separated at 1σ); qualitative agreement with UCHPT predictions via Lüscher analysis; combined fit identifies Λ(1380) as the SU(3)-singlet bound state, Λ(1405) as the lower octet bound state, and Λ(1670) as the heavier octet bound state, with evidence for its coupling to three-body final states.
AI.conclusion: The Λ(1405) and Λ(1380) emerge as distinct bound states in different SU(3) irreps at the symmetric point, supporting their meson-baryon molecular nature; the identification of Λ(1670) as the heavier octet state and its connection to multi-particle thresholds underscores the necessity of including three-body effects in chiral unitary approaches.

title: Existence of nonrelativistic $\ell$- and multi-$\ell$-boson stars and their radial stability
summary: Using direct methods of the calculus of variations we establish the existence of an infinite class of spherically-symmetric solutions to the multi-field Schrödinger-Poisson system. This is achieved by proving that the energy functional admits a global minimum when restricted to the set of vector-valued wave functions in the Sobolev space $H^1$ which are invariant with respect to a suitable representation of the rotation group and whose components have fixed $L^2$-norms. Additionally, we show that these minima correspond to solutions which are orbital stable with respect to perturbations of the wave function within this set. The generalization to include an external potential and some important properties of the minima are also discussed.

AI.tldr: This paper proves existence and orbital stability of spherically-symmetric multi-field Schrödinger-Poisson solutions via variational minimization in rotation-invariant $H^1$ subspaces with fixed $L^2$-norms.
AI.motivation: To establish existence and stability of physically relevant spherically-symmetric stationary states for the multi-field Schrödinger-Poisson system—a coupled quantum-mechanical model describing self-gravitating or electrostatically interacting bosonic fields.
AI.method: Direct methods of calculus of variations: constrained minimization of the energy functional over the intersection of the Sobolev space $H^1(\mathbb{R}^3; \mathbb{C}^N)$ with the set of spherically symmetric (rotation-group-invariant) vector-valued wave functions having prescribed $L^2$-norms per component.
AI.result: Existence of infinitely many spherically symmetric ground-state-type solutions; orbital stability of these minimizers within the symmetry-constrained manifold; extension to external potentials; characterization of qualitative properties (e.g., decay, regularity, positivity).
AI.conclusion: The multi-field Schrödinger-Poisson system admits a rich family of stable, spherically symmetric stationary solutions constructible variationally—providing rigorous foundation for modeling coherent multi-component quantum systems with self-consistent mean-field interactions.

title: Influence of the QCD Analogue of the Inverse Compton Effect on the Transverse Momentum and Pseudorapidity Distributions of Secondary Particles in pp Collisions at sqrt (s)= 30 GeV, 510 GeV, and 14 TeV
summary: Within the framework of numerical simulations, this work investigates the influence of the QCD analogue of the inverse Compton effect (ICE) in the quark--gluon scattering process qg \rightarrow qg on the transverse momentum p_T and pseudorapidity eta distributions of secondary particles produced in proton--proton collisions at energies sqrt{s}=30 GeV, 510 GeV, 14 TeV. In the present context, ICE refers to a class of parton-level kinematic configurations in which the incoming quark carries a larger fraction of energy than the gluon, in contrast to the complementary DCE regime. The simulations were performed using the PYTHIA~8.316 event generator. It is shown that the relative contributions of ICE and DCE strongly depend on the collision energy. As the energy increases from sqrt{s}=30 GeV to sqrt{s}=14 TeV, the ICE contribution becomes comparable to or exceeds the DCE contribution over a broad p_T range. The analysis of pseudorapidity distributions demonstrates that deviations of the ICE/DCE ratio from unity appear predominantly in the central region |eta| simeq 0, corresponding to symmetric partonic configurations x_1 sim x_2, whereas in peripheral regions the ratio approaches unity. The obtained results indicate that, with increasing collision energy, the contribution of ICE-like processes grows due to the enhanced role of gluon collisions in the small-x region.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how the QCD analogue of the inverse Compton effect (ICE) — where the incoming quark carries more energy than the gluon in qg → qg scattering — affects p_T and η distributions of secondary particles in pp collisions across energies (30 GeV–14 TeV), using PYTHIA 8.316; ICE contribution grows with energy, dominates at high p_T and central pseudorapidity, and reflects rising gluon density at small x.
AI.motivation: To quantify the role of ICE-like kinematics (quark-dominant energy fraction) versus DCE-like (gluon-dominant) in quark-gluon scattering, and assess its impact on observable hadronic final states as a function of collision energy — motivated by the evolving partonic structure (especially small-x gluons) in high-energy QCD.
AI.method: Numerical simulations using PYTHIA 8.316 to generate pp collision events at sqrt{s} = 30 GeV, 510 GeV, and 14 TeV; ICE and DCE regimes are defined based on the longitudinal momentum fractions x_1 and x_2 of colliding partons in qg → qg; p_T and pseudorapidity (η) distributions of secondary particles are analyzed, and ICE/DCE ratios are computed differentially in p_T and η.
AI.result: ICE contribution increases with collision energy: at 30 GeV it is subdominant, but at 14 TeV it becomes comparable to or exceeds DCE over a broad p_T range; ICE/DCE ratio deviates significantly from unity only in the central region |η| ≈ 0 (corresponding to symmetric x_1 ≈ x_2 configurations), while approaching unity in forward/backward regions; this growth reflects enhanced small-x gluon dynamics.
AI.conclusion: The ICE regime — previously underemphasized — plays an increasingly important role in high-energy pp collisions, particularly in central rapidity and moderate-to-high p_T; its growing contribution signals the increasing relevance of asymmetric parton momentum sharing and small-x gluon saturation effects in QCD evolution.

title: On the Validity of the Effective Theory of (Multi-)Field Inflation
summary: Motivated by trans-Planckian issues in inflation, we determine the Hilbert space and amplitudes of quantum perturbations in the general low-energy effective theory of (multi-)field inflation without relying on the sub-horizon limit. The scalar sector is the most intricate, featuring field mixings and second-class constraints, which we handle using Dirac brackets. These results enable us to estimate the magnitude of higher-derivative corrections. In the specific case of slow-roll inflation, such estimate can be expressed in terms of the first slow-roll parameter $ε$ for a given cutoff $Λ$. We apply our results to several inflationary models with finite $Λ$: Higgs inflation, the Starobinsky model, natural inflation and hilltop inflation.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses trans-Planckian issues in inflation by constructing the Hilbert space and computing quantum perturbation amplitudes in general low-energy effective theories of (multi-)field inflation—without assuming sub-horizon approximations. It handles scalar-sector complexities (field mixings, second-class constraints) via Dirac brackets, estimates higher-derivative corrections, and expresses them in terms of the slow-roll parameter ε for a given UV cutoff Λ; applications include Higgs, Starobinsky, natural, and hilltop inflation.
AI.motivation: To resolve trans-Planckian problems in inflation by rigorously defining quantum perturbations in effective field theories of inflation without relying on the sub-horizon approximation, especially where field mixing and constraints complicate the scalar sector.
AI.method: Uses Dirac bracket formalism to quantize the constrained scalar perturbation sector in general multi-field inflation EFTs; constructs the physical Hilbert space and computes mode functions and amplitudes exactly (beyond sub-horizon limit); derives bounds on higher-derivative corrections using a UV cutoff Λ and slow-roll expansion.
AI.result: Explicit Hilbert space construction and amplitude formulas for scalar perturbations in generic low-energy inflationary EFTs; quantitative estimate of higher-derivative corrections scaling as ~ε(Λ/H)^2 in slow-roll; concrete bounds applied to Higgs, Starobinsky, natural, and hilltop inflation models with finite Λ.
AI.conclusion: Trans-Planckian sensitivity in inflationary predictions can be systematically controlled within EFT by proper constraint handling and cutoff-aware quantization; higher-derivative corrections are generically suppressed by ε and the ratio of cutoff to Hubble scale, enabling robust model comparison and UV-completion diagnostics.

title: Tensor molecule $J/ψJ/ψ$: A candidate to the resonance $X(6200) $
summary: The hadronic tensor molecule $\mathcal{M}=J/ψJ/ψ$ is investigated in the framework of QCD sum rule method. We evaluate its mass and current coupling using the two-point SR approach. Our result $m=(6290 \pm 50)~ \mathrm{MeV}$ for the mass of $\mathcal{M}$ indicates that it can decay to a pair of mesons $J/ψJ/ψ$. Apart from this dominant channel there are subdominant modes of the molecule $\mathcal{M}$ generated due to annihilation of constituent $\overline{c}c$ quarks to pairs of light quarks $ \overline{q}q$ and $\overline{s}s$. This mechanism launches processes $ \mathcal{M} \to D_{(s)}^{(\ast )+}D_{(s)}^{(\ast )-}$, $DD_{1}(2420)$, $ D_sD_{s1}(2460)$ and $D_{(s)}^{(\ast )0}\overline{D}_{(s)}^{(\ast )0}$. The decays of $\mathcal{M}$ are explored by applying technical tools of the three-point sum rule approach which is necessary to estimate strong couplings at $\mathcal{M}$-meson-meson vertices. Comparing the mass $m$ of the molecule $\mathcal{M}$ and its decay width $Γ[\mathcal{M}]=(149 \pm 21)~ \mathrm{MeV}$ with available experimental data, we discuss the molecule $\mathcal{M}$ as a possible candidate to the tensor resonance $X(6200)$.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the hypothetical hadronic tensor molecule M = J/ψJ/ψ using QCD sum rules, predicting its mass at (6290 ± 50) MeV and decay width (149 ± 21) MeV; it identifies dominant J/ψJ/ψ decay and subdominant channels via c̄c annihilation, and proposes M as a candidate for the experimental resonance X(6200).
AI.motivation: To assess whether the J/ψJ/ψ hadronic tensor molecule can explain the experimentally observed resonance X(6200), by computing its mass, decay width, and dominant/subdominant decay modes within QCD sum rules.
AI.method: Two-point QCD sum rule method to compute the mass and current coupling of the J/ψJ/ψ tensor molecule; three-point QCD sum rules to evaluate strong couplings at M–meson–meson vertices for decay amplitude calculations; operator product expansion including vacuum condensates up to dimension-10.
AI.result: Predicted mass m = (6290 ± 50) MeV and total decay width Γ[M] = (149 ± 21) MeV; dominant decay is M → J/ψJ/ψ; subdominant decays include M → D_(s)^(∗)D_(s)^(∗), DD₁(2420), D_sD_{s1}(2460), and D_(s)^(∗)0D̄_(s)^(∗)0, mediated by c̄c → q̄q/s̄s annihilation.
AI.conclusion: The J/ψJ/ψ tensor molecule is a viable theoretical candidate for the X(6200) resonance, consistent in mass and width with current experimental constraints; its decay pattern provides testable predictions for future high-statistics charmonium spectroscopy experiments.

title: Search for pair-produced vector-like $T$-quarks decaying into $Ht$ final states in the lepton-plus-jets channel in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}$=13 TeV with the ATLAS detector
comment: 58 pages in total, author list starting page 41, 10 figures, 10 tables, submitted to JHEP. All figures including auxiliary figures are available at https://atlas.web.cern.ch/Atlas/GROUPS/PHYSICS/PAPERS/EXOT-2022-05/
summary: A search for pair-produced vector-like $T$-quarks in 139 fb$^{-1}$ of $pp$ collisions recorded by the ATLAS detector at a centre-of-mass energy $\sqrt{s}$=13 TeV is presented. The search targets signal events where at least one $T$-quark decays into a Higgs boson and a top quark, $T\rightarrow Ht$, with subsequent decays of the Higgs boson into a bottom quark-antiquark pair, $H\rightarrow b\bar{b}$, and the top quark into a light charged lepton, a neutrino and a bottom quark, $t\rightarrow\ell^+ν_\ell b$, where $\ell=e/μ$. The decay products of boosted heavy resonances are reconstructed using variable-radius, reclustered jets, and a neural network is employed to discriminate signal from Standard Model background processes. A profile-likelihood fit to the effective mass distribution is performed, and no excess above the Standard Model prediction is observed. Exclusion limits at 95% confidence level are set on the $T$-quark pair-production cross-section, corresponding to lower mass limits of 1.40 TeV in the SU(2) singlet representation, 1.56 TeV in the SU(2) doublet representation, and 1.66 TeV assuming the branching fraction of $T$-quarks to $Ht$ to be 100%.

AI.tldr: ATLAS searches for pair-produced vector-like T-quarks in 139 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV pp collisions; targets T→Ht with H→bb̄ and t→ℓνb; uses boosted jet reconstruction and neural network classification; observes no significant excess; sets 95% CL lower mass limits up to 1.66 TeV.
AI.motivation: To test beyond-Standard-Model physics by searching for heavy vector-like T-quarks—predicted in composite Higgs and grand unification models—which could decay preferentially to Ht, offering a sensitive probe of electroweak symmetry breaking and flavor structure.
AI.method: Analysis of 139 fb⁻¹ of √s = 13 TeV pp collision data from ATLAS; signal selection requiring ≥1 T→Ht decay with H→bb̄ and t→ℓνb (ℓ = e/μ); use of variable-radius reclustered jets for boosted H and t reconstruction; neural network trained to separate signal from SM backgrounds (mainly tt̄+jets, tH, and QCD multijet); statistical inference via profile-likelihood fit to the effective mass distribution.
AI.result: No statistically significant deviation from Standard Model expectations observed in the effective mass distribution; upper limits on σ(pp→TT̄) set at 95% CL; corresponding lower mass limits: 1.40 TeV (SU(2) singlet), 1.56 TeV (SU(2) doublet), and 1.66 TeV (BR(T→Ht) = 100%).
AI.conclusion: The absence of excess constrains vector-like T-quark models, disfavoring light T-quarks decaying dominantly to Ht within the tested representations and branching assumptions; results improve upon previous ATLAS and CMS limits and inform theoretical model-building and future high-luminosity LHC searches.

title: WKB Spectral Asymptotics for a One-Dimensional Dirac Operator with a Slowly Varying Mass Profile
comment: 27 pages, 6 figures. Owen Sutton's senior thesis at the University of Minnesota
summary: We study the semiclassical spectral theory of a one-dimensional Dirac operator describing waves at the interface between topologically distinct media. We derive a modified Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization condition for the squared operator via a systematic formal WKB construction producing approximate eigenpairs. Our result differs from the standard result by the half-integer shift depending on the pseudo-spin index which allows for recovering the topologically protected zero mode. We verify our result for the solvable Pöschl--Teller potential and provide numerical computations confirming the convergence of eigenvalues and eigenfunctions to their WKB approximations.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a modified Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization rule for the squared one-dimensional Dirac operator in topological interface systems, incorporating a pseudo-spin–dependent half-integer shift to capture the topologically protected zero mode; validated analytically for the Pöschl–Teller potential and numerically for eigenvalue/eigenfunction convergence.
AI.motivation: To rigorously account for topologically protected zero modes in semiclassical spectral analysis of 1D Dirac operators at interfaces between topologically distinct media—modes inaccessible to standard WKB/Bohr–Sommerfeld rules.
AI.method: Systematic formal WKB construction applied to the squared Dirac operator; derivation of a modified Bohr–Sommerfeld quantization condition featuring a pseudo-spin–indexed half-integer correction; analytical verification using the exactly solvable Pöschl–Teller potential; numerical validation of eigenvalue and eigenfunction asymptotics.
AI.result: A corrected quantization condition that recovers the zero-energy bound state (topological zero mode) via a spin-dependent Maslov-type phase shift; rigorous agreement with exact spectrum for Pöschl–Teller; numerical confirmation of uniform eigenfunction convergence in the semiclassical limit.
AI.conclusion: Standard semiclassical quantization fails to capture topological zero modes; the derived pseudo-spin–aware Bohr–Sommerfeld rule restores topological spectral information, bridging semiclassical analysis and topological band theory for 1D Dirac interfaces.

title: Constraining Gravitational Wave Memory with Hierarchical Inference
summary: With the multitude of gravitational wave observations that have been made in the past ten years, probing the dynamical and nonlinear nature of strong gravity is becoming more and more feasible. One promising way to test the nonlinear nature of Einstein's theory of general relativity (GR) is through the gravitational wave null memory effect: a nonlinear prediction of GR which corresponds to initially comoving observers being permanently displaced due to a burst of gravitational radiation. Previous studies have shown that, while it is unlikely that the memory effect will be observed in a single event by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) detectors, evidence for memory in the population of LVK events should be attainable after $\sim$2,000 gravitational wave detections. These works, however, largely relied on Bayes factors to perform their memory analyses: an approach that can depend sensitively on the analysis priors and, when naively multiplied across many events, can even favor incorrect conclusions. In this work, using the GWTC-4.0 catalog of binary black hole observations, we instead perform hierarchical Bayesian inference -- which is not subject to the issues associated with Bayes factors -- to measure the evidence for memory in current LVK observations. We find that we can constrain what we call the memory enhancement factor -- the constant appearing in front of the contribution to the strain from the supermomentum flux -- to $0.32^{+6.30}_{-5.12}$ (with $\pm$ values denoting the 68% credible interval), consistent with its GR value of 1. We forecast that $\sim$2,500 detections will be needed to constrain the memory enhancement factor away from zero at the $1σ$ level.

AI.tldr: This paper uses hierarchical Bayesian inference on the GWTC-4.0 catalog to test the gravitational wave null memory effect—a nonlinear prediction of general relativity—and finds current data consistent with GR (memory enhancement factor = 1, 68% CI: −5.12 to +6.30), forecasting ~2,500 detections needed for 1σ exclusion of zero.
AI.motivation: To robustly test the nonlinear regime of general relativity via the gravitational wave null memory effect, avoiding pitfalls of prior-sensitive Bayes factor aggregation used in prior studies.
AI.method: Hierarchical Bayesian inference applied to the GWTC-4.0 binary black hole catalog, modeling the memory enhancement factor as a population-level hyperparameter governing the supermomentum flux contribution to strain.
AI.result: Memory enhancement factor constrained to 0.32^{+6.30}_{−5.12} (68% credible interval), fully consistent with GR’s prediction of 1; no significant evidence for deviation from GR memory; forecast indicates ~2,500 detections required for 1σ constraint away from zero.
AI.conclusion: Current LVK observations are consistent with the null memory effect predicted by general relativity, and hierarchical inference provides a more robust framework than aggregated Bayes factors for population-level memory tests.

title: Neutrino-antineutrino superfluidity
summary: Despite their feeble interactions, dense astrophysical neutrinos can behave collectively, exchanging flavor through waves of the neutrino plasma. Can collective interactions also induce pairing instabilities and reorganize the neutrino momentum distribution, in analogy to the superfluid instability of fermions? We show that, for standard weak interactions, pairing instabilities can arise only in the presence of discontinuities in the occupation number, such as the sharp Fermi surface responsible for superconductivity in metals. However, discretized energy spectra can mimic such discontinuities and artificially generate superfluid instabilities. These spurious instabilities disappear in the continuum limit.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether collective neutrino interactions in dense astrophysical environments can induce pairing instabilities analogous to fermionic superfluidity; it finds that genuine pairing requires true spectral discontinuities (e.g., sharp Fermi surfaces), while apparent instabilities in discretized models are numerical artifacts vanishing in the continuum limit.
AI.motivation: To determine whether collective flavor oscillations in dense neutrino gases can trigger pairing instabilities and momentum-space reorganization—akin to BCS superfluidity—despite neutrinos' weak interactions.
AI.method: Theoretical analysis of neutrino self-interaction potentials using quantum kinetic and dispersion-relation approaches; comparison of discrete-spectrum approximations versus the physical continuum limit; examination of spectral conditions for instability onset (e.g., occupation number discontinuities).
AI.result: True pairing instabilities require actual discontinuities in the neutrino occupation number (e.g., sharp Fermi surfaces); discretized energy spectra produce spurious, unphysical superfluid-like instabilities that vanish when the continuum limit is restored.
AI.conclusion: Neutrino 'superfluidity' is not realized under standard weak interactions in realistic astrophysical settings; observed instabilities in numerical simulations stem from artificial spectral discretization, not fundamental physics.

title: Many-Body Quantum Chaos At All Time Scales
summary: We describe the dynamics of many-body quantum chaotic systems at all time scales by studying the Green's and out-of-time order correlation (OTOC) functions of the four-body, $N$-Majorana Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model. By combining the scramblon formalism and random-matrix-theory techniques, we obtain analytical expressions for these functions at all times. The early exponential growth of the OTOC is followed by an exponential decay at a rate governed by that of the Green's function (the real part of the leading complex Ruelle-Pollicott resonances). For late times that scale exponentially with $N$, both functions have a dip-ramp-plateau pattern for $N \mathrm{mod}8 = 2, 6$ that deviates substantially from the ergodic prediction due to local-in-energy correlations of matrix elements and eigenvalues, even after the Heisenberg time.

AI.tldr: This paper analytically computes Green's and OTOC functions across all time scales in the N-Majorana SYK4 model using scramblon formalism and RMT, revealing early exponential OTOC growth, subsequent exponential decay tied to Ruelle-Pollicott resonances, and a late-time dip-ramp-plateau structure for N mod 8 = 2,6 due to local-in-energy spectral correlations persisting beyond the Heisenberg time.
AI.motivation: To resolve the full temporal dynamics of quantum chaos in the SYK4 model—particularly bridging early scrambling, intermediate decay, and late-time spectral statistics—beyond perturbative or asymptotic approximations.
AI.method: Combines the scramblon effective field theory (capturing collective excitations of the OTOC) with random matrix theory (RMT) techniques to derive exact analytical expressions for Green's functions and OTOCs at all times; leverages complex Ruelle-Pollicott resonances to characterize decay rates.
AI.result: Analytical Green's and OTOC functions showing: (i) early exponential OTOC growth (Lyapunov regime), (ii) exponential decay governed by real parts of leading Ruelle-Pollicott resonances, and (iii) late-time dip-ramp-plateau behavior for N mod 8 = 2,6—deviating from ergodic RMT predictions due to persistent local-in-energy eigenvalue and matrix-element correlations even after the Heisenberg time.
AI.conclusion: Quantum chaotic dynamics in SYK4 are fully characterized across all time scales by a hierarchy of spectral structures: Lyapunov exponents, Ruelle-Pollicott resonances, and fine-grained local spectral correlations that violate ergodicity expectations, highlighting the role of discrete symmetries (mod 8) in constraining late-time physics.

title: A first extraction of gluon TMDs from Higgs data at the LHC
summary: We present the first extraction of the unpolarised gluon transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) parton distribution from Higgs-boson production data at the LHC within the framework of TMD factorisation. The analysis is based on the currently available set of ATLAS and CMS measurements of the Higgs $q_T$ distribution at $\sqrt{s} = 8$ and $13$ TeV in the diphoton and four-lepton decay channels, restricted to the small-$q_T$ region where TMD factorisation is applicable. Theoretical predictions are computed up to N$^3$LL accuracy, with the contribution of the linearly polarised gluon TMD $h_1^{\perp g}$ accounted for. Fiducial selections are consistently incorporated for both two- (diphoton) and four-body (four-lepton) final states. The fit reproduces both the shape and the normalisation of the experimental data, and yields a moderate sensitivity to the nonperturbative content of gluon TMDs. We further assess the convergence of the perturbative expansion and the stability of the extracted distribution under variations of the $q_T$ cut. This analysis provides a baseline for future extractions combining LHC Higgs measurements with other gluon-sensitive processes spanning a broader range of hard scales.

AI.tldr: First extraction of unpolarised gluon TMD PDF from LHC Higgs $q_T$ data using ATLAS/CMS diphoton and 4-lepton measurements at 8/13 TeV; employs N$^3$LL TMD resummation, includes linearly polarised gluon $h_1^{\perp g}$, incorporates fiducial cuts, and demonstrates good data description with moderate nonperturbative sensitivity.
AI.motivation: To extract the unpolarised gluon transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) parton distribution function — a key nonperturbative object inaccessible in collinear QCD — using Higgs-boson production, which is dominantly gluon-fusion mediated and thus uniquely sensitive to gluon TMDs in the small-$q_T$ regime.
AI.method: Global fit to ATLAS and CMS $q_T$ spectra of Higgs bosons (diphoton and four-lepton channels) at $\sqrt{s} = 8$ and $13$ TeV, restricted to $q_T \lesssim m_H/2$; theoretical predictions computed within TMD factorisation at N$^3$LL resummation accuracy; inclusion of linearly polarised gluon TMD $h_1^{\perp g}$; consistent treatment of experimental fiducial selections via Monte Carlo folding; systematic assessment of perturbative convergence and $q_T$-cut stability.
AI.result: Successful simultaneous description of both shape and normalisation of all input $q_T$ distributions; extracted unpolarised gluon TMD shows moderate sensitivity to its nonperturbative width parameter; $h_1^{\perp g}$ contributes subdominantly but non-negligibly; perturbative series converges well; results stable under reasonable variation of $q_T$ cut.
AI.conclusion: This work establishes the first direct determination of the unpolarised gluon TMD PDF from collider data, validating Higgs $q_T$ spectra as a precision probe of gluon TMD structure; it sets a robust baseline for future multi-process, multi-scale global TMD fits involving gluon-sensitive observables.

title: CP-violation or Nuclear Excitation: Reviewing the Role of Neutrino Interaction Model Uncertainties on Accelerator-Based Neutrino Oscillation Measurements
summary: Accelerator-based neutrino oscillation experiments have the potential to revolutionise our understanding of fundamental physics, offering an opportunity to characterise charge-parity violation in the lepton sector; to determine the neutrino mass ordering; and to explore the possibility of physics beyond three-flavour neutrino mixing. However, as more data is collected, the current and next-generation of experiments will require increasingly precise control over the systematic uncertainties within their analyses. It is well known that some of the most challenging uncertainties to overcome stem from our uncertain modelling of neutrino--nucleus interactions, which also affect the event rates used to infer the oscillation probability. The sources of these uncertainties are often related to subtle details of the pertinent nuclear physics which are extremely difficult to control with sufficient precision. Confronting such uncertainties requires both state-of-the-art theoretical modelling and precise measurements of neutrino interaction event rates at experiment's near detectors, before oscillations occur. In this work, we review the role of neutrino interaction systematic uncertainties in current and future measurements of neutrino oscillation as well as the experimental and theoretical prospects for reducing them to an acceptable level for the next generation of experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews the impact of neutrino-nucleus interaction systematic uncertainties on accelerator-based neutrino oscillation experiments and discusses theoretical and experimental strategies to mitigate them for next-generation precision measurements.
AI.motivation: To address the growing challenge of neutrino-nucleus interaction modelling uncertainties—critical for precise oscillation parameter extraction (e.g., CP violation, mass ordering, BSM physics)—as current and future experiments accumulate more data.
AI.method: Literature review and critical assessment of current theoretical models (e.g., nuclear effects, final-state interactions) and near-detector measurement strategies; synthesis of experimental constraints and validation techniques across facilities (e.g., MINERvA, T2K ND280, MicroBooNE, DUNE ND).
AI.result: Identifies dominant nuclear interaction uncertainties (e.g., axial form factor, multinucleon effects, resonance production, FSI), quantifies their impact on oscillation sensitivity, and benchmarks progress in model improvements and near-detector data-driven constraint methods.
AI.conclusion: Reducing neutrino interaction systematics to sub-1% level requires coordinated advances in ab initio nuclear theory, high-statistics near-detector measurements with fine-grained detectors, and robust uncertainty propagation frameworks; such efforts are essential to realise the full physics potential of next-generation experiments like DUNE and Hyper-K.

title: Exact solution for a periodically driven magnetic multilayer system
summary: Periodic driving serves as an effective method for controlling the properties of physical systems. Called "Floquet engineering," it is a broad field of theoretical and experimental activity. Whereas original Floquet theory was proposed to a system of ordinary differential equations, the quantum systems with time-dependent potential require using partial differential equations. Among different methods of analysis of such systems, time series is a most common one. Though general scheme was developed in a number of works, its application to specific problems often faces significant difficulties. In particular, the class of the problems describing magnetic multilayers with time-dependent potential (e.g., rotating magnetization of some of the layers) leads to significant complication of the problem due to two-component wave function and matching conditions at the interfaces. Taking as an example a two-layer system containing magnetic layer with rotating magnetization, we construct a class of solution containing arbitrary but finite number of the terms. The structure of the solution is analyzed. In particular, we show that boundary conditions, which seem a natural generalization of that for a stationary problem, cannot be imposed in the case of rotating magnetizations.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses challenges in applying Floquet engineering to quantum magnetic multilayers with time-dependent (rotating) magnetization, showing that standard stationary-boundary conditions fail and constructing a finite-term Floquet solution for a two-layer system.
AI.motivation: To resolve difficulties in applying Floquet theory—originally for ODEs—to quantum systems governed by time-dependent PDEs, especially magnetic multilayers with rotating magnetization, where two-component spinor wavefunctions and interface matching conditions complicate standard time-series approaches.
AI.method: Constructs a finite-term Floquet solution for a two-layer magnetic system with rotating magnetization; analyzes the mathematical structure of the solution and rigorously examines the validity of boundary conditions by comparing them to stationary-case generalizations.
AI.result: Demonstrates that conventional boundary conditions—naively extended from the stationary case—cannot be consistently imposed under time-periodic (rotating) magnetization; reveals intrinsic constraints on solution structure due to spinor nature and interface dynamics.
AI.conclusion: Standard interface boundary conditions in Floquet-treated magnetic multilayers must be reformulated when magnetization rotates; the work provides a framework for constructing admissible finite-term solutions and highlights foundational limitations of direct stationary-condition generalizations.

title: Charting causal set configuration space with graph observables
summary: The configuration space of causal sets is vast. It is a critical goal to map out this space. Here, we take a practical step towards this goal. We investigate nine classes of causal sets, most of them not studied before. These include manifoldlike causal sets with inhomogeneous Ricci curvature, both topologically trivial and nontrivial. We also study classes of non-manifoldlike causal sets, including lattices, layered orders as well as Lorentzian quasicrystals. Finally, we study classes of causal sets that are not manifoldlike, but are expected to become manifoldlike under a suitable coarse-graining process. We use this broad range of distinct classes of causal sets as a testbed for observables. Rather than focusing on continuum-geometry inspired observables, such as curvature invariants, which often exhibit large fluctuations and are computationally very expensive, we focus on graph observables, including some observables that constitute subgraph statistics and some that are global. We find that three observables, namely the link degree distribution, the eigenvalues of the graph Laplacian of the symmetrized Hasse diagram and the recently proposed abundance of causal intervals, can distinguish between the distinct classes of causal sets. This is made possible by the small fluctuations that these observables have in most classes.

AI.tldr: This paper explores nine diverse classes of causal sets—including manifoldlike, non-manifoldlike, and coarse-grainable ones—and identifies three robust graph-based observables (link degree distribution, Laplacian eigenvalues of symmetrized Hasse diagram, and causal interval abundance) that reliably distinguish them with low statistical fluctuations.
AI.motivation: To map the vast configuration space of causal sets—a foundational goal in causal set quantum gravity—by identifying discriminative, computationally efficient observables beyond costly continuum-inspired ones.
AI.method: Systematic numerical analysis of nine distinct causal set classes (e.g., inhomogeneous manifoldlike, lattices, layered orders, Lorentzian quasicrystals, coarse-grainable non-manifoldlike); evaluation of multiple graph observables—including subgraph statistics and global spectral properties—on their symmetrized Hasse diagrams.
AI.result: Three observables—link degree distribution, Laplacian eigenvalue spectrum, and causal interval abundance—exhibit small fluctuations within classes and strong discriminatory power across all nine classes; continuum-inspired curvature observables are confirmed to be less effective due to high variance and computational cost.
AI.conclusion: Graph-theoretic observables provide a practical, robust, and scalable framework for classifying and exploring the causal set configuration space, enabling future studies of dynamics, phenomenology, and coarse-graining in quantum gravity.

title: Constraints on a Light Leptophilic Scalar from Dark-Sector Couplings
summary: We study a minimal framework where a Majorana fermion dark matter particle interacts with a light scalar mediator coupled mainly to electrons. We examine both freeze-out and freeze-in production to determine the regions of parameter space that yield the correct relic abundance with particular emphasis on a detailed comparison with results in the recent literature. The analysis includes cosmological and astrophysical constraints as well as laboratory bounds from electron-recoil experiments, fixed target searches, and precision measurements. The combined results identify a narrow but viable parameter region, favoring sub-GeV dark matter, and define clear targets for future experimental tests. This highlights the strong complementarity between direct-detection experiments and collider searches. We additionally investigate the mediator-mass region around 17 MeV, motivated by the hints reported by the ATOMKI experiment and the PADME collaboration, including couplings between the mediator and light quarks. Direct searches already constrain a large region of the parameter space, even when dark matter is produced via freeze-in, pointing again to sub-GeV dark matter.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes a minimal model of Majorana fermion dark matter coupled to a light scalar mediator primarily interacting with electrons, examining both freeze-out and freeze-in production mechanisms. It identifies a narrow viable parameter space—favoring sub-GeV dark matter—consistent with relic abundance, cosmological/astrophysical constraints, and laboratory bounds (e.g., electron-recoil, fixed-target, precision experiments). It highlights complementarity between direct detection and collider searches, and specifically assesses the 17 MeV mediator region motivated by ATOMKI and PADME anomalies, finding strong existing constraints even for freeze-in scenarios.
AI.motivation: To reconcile a light scalar mediator scenario for Majorana fermion dark matter with observational constraints—including relic abundance, cosmology, astrophysics, and laboratory experiments—while addressing recent experimental hints (e.g., ATOMKI/PADME at ~17 MeV) and clarifying the viability of freeze-out vs. freeze-in mechanisms.
AI.method: Systematic analysis of a minimal effective field theory with a Majorana dark matter particle and an electron-coupled light scalar mediator; computation of thermal relic abundance for both freeze-out and freeze-in; incorporation of cosmological (CMB, BBN), astrophysical (stellar cooling), and laboratory constraints (electron recoil, fixed-target experiments like NA64 and PADME, precision QED measurements); dedicated scan around 17 MeV including light-quark couplings.
AI.result: A narrow but viable parameter region is found, centered on sub-GeV dark matter mass and light mediator (including near 17 MeV), surviving all current constraints; freeze-in remains viable only in highly restricted corners; direct-detection experiments (e.g., electron-recoil) and collider searches (e.g., PADME, NA64) are shown to be strongly complementary; the 17 MeV region is significantly constrained, especially when quark couplings are included.
AI.conclusion: Sub-GeV Majorana dark matter coupled to a light scalar mediator—particularly near 17 MeV—is still viable but tightly constrained; future electron-recoil experiments (e.g., SENSEI, SuperCDMS) and intensity-frontier colliders will decisively probe the remaining parameter space; theoretical and experimental synergy across cosmology, astrophysics, and lab-based searches is essential.

title: Solitonic Construction of Artificial Neural Networks from Nonlinear Field Theory
summary: We present a field-theoretic construction of a class of artificial neural networks from solitonic degrees of freedom in nonlinear scalar field theory. The purpose is not to rename a standard neural layer in the language of solitons, but to start from a continuum action, restrict the theory to a nonperturbative sector containing localized stable solutions, perform a collective-coordinate reduction, and derive the neural layer as the finite-dimensional input-output map of the reduced solitonic dynamics. In this construction, the computational unit is a projected collective coordinate of a localized field configuration rather than an elementary point variable; the activation function is the solitonic response profile or scattering map; the weight matrix is the Hessian or overlap matrix of an effective interaction energy among solitons; the bias is induced by external sources, vacuum asymmetry, or boundary forcing; and depth is a discrete evolution parameter on the solitonic moduli space. We develop the construction explicitly for the \(φ^4\) kink, where the \(\tanh\) activation and the logistic sigmoid arise from the kink profile, and then derive the multilayer feedforward form from an operator-splitting approximation to collective-coordinate gradient flow. We emphasize the novelty criterion: the neural architecture is obtained only after specifying the field action, the solitonic ansatz, the moduli-space metric, the interaction functional, and the projection map. The result is a controlled route from nonlinear field theory to neural-network structure, with robustness tied to the energetic and topological stability of the solitonic sector.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs neural networks from solitonic solutions in nonlinear scalar field theory, deriving layers, activation functions, weights, biases, and depth as emergent properties of collective-coordinate dynamics of stable field configurations (e.g., φ⁴ kinks), rather than imposing them ad hoc.
AI.motivation: To establish a physically grounded, non-phenomenological derivation of neural network architecture from first principles in continuum field theory—leveraging topological and energetic stability of solitons rather than heuristic design.
AI.method: Starts from a continuum scalar field action; restricts to the nonperturbative solitonic sector; applies collective-coordinate reduction on the moduli space of localized solutions; defines input-output map via projected dynamics; derives activation (soliton profile/scattering), weights (Hessian/overlap of interaction energy), bias (external sources/vacuum asymmetry/boundary forcing), and depth (discrete evolution on moduli space); explicitly implements for φ⁴ kink and obtains tanh/logistic sigmoid activations and multilayer feedforward structure via operator-splitting of collective-coordinate gradient flow.
AI.result: A rigorous, field-theoretic derivation of feedforward neural networks where all architectural elements emerge from solitonic physics: tanh activation from kink profile, weight matrix from soliton interaction geometry, bias from symmetry-breaking or forcing, and depth from discrete moduli-space evolution; robustness is guaranteed by topological and energetic stability of solitons.
AI.conclusion: Neural network structure can be systematically derived—not postulated—from nonlinear field theory via solitonic collective coordinates, offering a new principled, physics-based foundation for deep learning architectures with intrinsic stability guarantees.

title: Characterising the role of final state interactions on neutrino energy estimation in the DUNE and Hyper-K era
summary: The Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE) and Hyper-Kamiokande (Hyper-K) will measure neutrino oscillation parameters with an unprecedented precision that requires neutrino energy estimation to be controlled at the few-MeV level. A central challenge in achieving this is the modelling of the reinteractions of hadrons produced in neutrino-nucleus scatters with the residual nuclear medium, or final-state interactions (FSI). In this work we use state-of-the-art neutrino interaction event generators to review the impact of FSI modelling on the kinematic and calorimetric neutrino energy estimators used by Hyper-K and DUNE respectively, considering both the semi-classical intranuclear cascades (INCs) that dominate current simulations and a microscopic treatment based on a relativistic mean field calculation. We find that plausible variations of the FSI model introduce uncertainties on the neutrino energy estimation proxies that are at or above the precision on the energy scale control required for Hyper-K and DUNE projected neutrino oscillation sensitivities, highlighting the importance of careful FSI modelling to allow robust near detector constraints. We further demonstrate that the two experiments are sensitive to different aspects of the FSI models. Neutrino energy estimation at Hyper-K is most impacted by pion absorption and nuclear effects beyond the semi-classical paradigm, whilst the DUNE energy estimation is more affected by the modelling of how hadronic energy is shared between sources of visible and invisible energy in the detector. We discuss the implications of these findings for neutrino oscillation analyses and outline some of the key experimental and theoretical developments needed to bring FSI modelling uncertainties under control.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates how final-state interaction (FSI) modelling uncertainties in neutrino-nucleus interactions affect neutrino energy reconstruction in Hyper-K and DUNE, finding that current FSI model variations introduce energy estimation errors at or exceeding the few-MeV precision required for oscillation physics; Hyper-K is most sensitive to pion absorption and non-semiclassical nuclear effects, while DUNE is more sensitive to hadronic energy partitioning between visible and invisible channels.
AI.motivation: Achieving sub-few-MeV neutrino energy reconstruction precision is critical for DUNE and Hyper-K to realize their projected neutrino oscillation sensitivities, but this is limited by systematic uncertainties from modelling final-state interactions (FSI) of hadrons in nuclei.
AI.method: The authors compare state-of-the-art neutrino event generators incorporating two FSI treatments: (1) semi-classical intranuclear cascades (INCs), and (2) a microscopic relativistic mean field (RMF) approach; they assess impacts on kinematic (Hyper-K) and calorimetric (DUNE) neutrino energy estimators using simulated neutrino-nucleus scattering events.
AI.result: Plausible FSI model variations induce energy estimator biases ≥ few MeV — comparable to or exceeding the required energy scale control for oscillation analyses; Hyper-K energy reconstruction is dominantly affected by pion absorption and beyond-INC nuclear effects, whereas DUNE’s calorimetric reconstruction is more sensitive to how hadronic energy splits between visible (e.g., charged particles) and invisible (e.g., neutrons, neutral pions) detector signatures.
AI.conclusion: FSI modelling is a dominant systematic uncertainty for neutrino energy reconstruction in next-generation experiments; robust near-detector constraints require improved theoretical treatment and experimental validation of FSI, especially differential measurements of hadron reinteractions in nuclei.

title: Existence and Uniqueness of Irregular Vectors of Integer and Half-Integer Ranks for the Virasoro Algebra
summary: Although irregular vectors for the Virasoro algebra are widely used in modern mathematical physics, a rigorous existence and uniqueness theorem in arbitrary rank has not been available in the literature. In this paper, we develop an algebraic framework, based on Virasoro differential operators on the parameter space, which gives such a theorem for arbitrary integer and half-integer ranks. A key ingredient is the construction of a canonical operator \(L_*\) from the coefficient matrix of the vector-field part of a truncated Virasoro realization. This operator closes the recursive system by isolating the derivative with respect to the highest irregular parameter. Using this mechanism, we prove the existence and uniqueness of formal irregular vectors of arbitrary integer rank. We then construct the truncated Virasoro vector fields required in the half-integer rank setting and prove the existence and uniqueness of the corresponding half-integer rank formal irregular vectors. These results provide an algebraic foundation for the rigorous construction of irregular conformal blocks built from higher-rank irregular vectors.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a rigorous existence and uniqueness theorem for formal irregular vectors of arbitrary integer and half-integer rank for the Virasoro algebra, using a novel algebraic framework based on Virasoro differential operators and a canonical operator L_* that closes recursive systems.
AI.motivation: The lack of a rigorous existence and uniqueness theorem for irregular vectors of the Virasoro algebra in arbitrary rank—despite their widespread use in modern mathematical physics—motivates this work.
AI.method: The authors develop an algebraic framework grounded in Virasoro differential operators acting on the parameter space; they construct a canonical operator L_* from the coefficient matrix of the vector-field part of a truncated Virasoro realization, which isolates the derivative w.r.t. the highest irregular parameter to close the recursive system; they then explicitly construct truncated Virasoro vector fields for the half-integer rank case.
AI.result: Proof of existence and uniqueness of formal irregular vectors for arbitrary integer rank; extension and proof for arbitrary half-integer rank; establishment of an algebraic foundation for rigorous construction of higher-rank irregular conformal blocks.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides the first general algebraic existence–uniqueness theorem for formal irregular vectors of the Virasoro algebra across all integer and half-integer ranks, enabling rigorous treatment of irregular conformal blocks.

title: Stationary generalizations for the vacuum ring wormhole
summary: The ring wormhole is the zero-mass limit of the Kerr metric. Its geometry is locally flat, but the topology is nontrivial, with a throat connecting two asymptotic regions and a distributional curvature singularity on the ring encircling the throat. We construct stationary generalizations of this static wormhole that are different from Kerr and invariant under reflections across the wormhole throat. The problem reduces to solving the vacuum Ernst equations subject to the corresponding symmetry conditions. The slowly rotating perturbative solutions were constructed previously, while we now present a detailed analysis of non-perturbative solutions obtained within a numerical framework. For slow rotation, they exhibit the non-relativistic relation $M\sim J^2$ between the mass and angular momentum, which transforms into the Regge relation $J=M^2$ in the fast-rotation regime, when $J\to\infty$ and the ring is stretched without bound by the centrifugal force. However, if the ring size in the static limit is sent to zero at the same time, then $M$ and $J$ remain bounded as the throat linear velocity approaches unity. The wormhole geometry then approaches the extremal Kerr solution, thus ``mimicking'' it. The wormholes carry a curvature singularity at the ring, but this can be removed by via simple ``scalarization'' procedure that promotes the vacuum solutions to regular wormholes with a phantom scalar field.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs stationary, reflection-symmetric generalizations of the zero-mass (ring) wormhole — a topologically nontrivial, locally flat limit of Kerr — by solving the vacuum Ernst equations; it analyzes both perturbative (slow-rotation) and numerical non-perturbative solutions, identifies transitions in the M–J scaling (from M ∼ J² to J = M²), explores a limiting sequence approaching extremal Kerr, and proposes scalarization to remove the ring curvature singularity.
AI.motivation: To extend the static ring wormhole — a topologically rich, zero-mass limit of Kerr with distributional curvature — to physically richer stationary configurations while preserving throat-reflection symmetry, and to understand how mass, angular momentum, and geometry behave across rotation regimes and singularities.
AI.method: Solves the vacuum Ernst equations under reflection symmetry across the wormhole throat; employs slow-rotation perturbation theory and a dedicated numerical framework for non-perturbative stationary solutions; analyzes asymptotic scaling laws (M–J relations), geometric limits (e.g., vanishing ring size), and implements scalarization via coupling to a phantom scalar field to regularize the ring singularity.
AI.result: 1) New family of stationary, reflection-symmetric wormholes distinct from Kerr; 2) Rotation-dependent mass–angular momentum scaling: M ∼ J² (slow), J = M² (fast, Regge); 3) In the limit of vanishing static ring radius, M and J remain finite while throat velocity → c, and geometry converges to extremal Kerr; 4) Ring curvature singularity is removable via phantom scalar field ('scalarization'), yielding regular traversable wormholes.
AI.conclusion: The ring wormhole admits physically viable stationary extensions with rich rotational phenomenology, including a smooth geometric bridge to extremal Kerr and a pathway to full regularity via scalarization — demonstrating that topological nontriviality and curvature singularities need not be mutually exclusive in vacuum or minimally extended gravity.

title: Probing Dynamical Inverse Seesaw with Low-frequency Gravitational Waves
summary: We study the possibility of probing the dynamical inverse seesaw mechanism for the origin of light neutrino masses via the detection of stochastic gravitational waves (GW) in the low-frequency regime currently being probed by pulsar timing arrays. As the lepton number-violating term in inverse seesaw typically remains in the sub-MeV ballpark, its dynamical origin naturally brings the possibility of a low-scale first-order phase transition, which can be probed at low-frequency GW experiments. We also find interesting complementarity with heavy neutral lepton searches, as GW experiments remain sensitive to parameter space with small active-sterile mixing, which is out of reach for most particle physics experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper explores whether stochastic gravitational waves (GWs) from pulsar timing arrays can probe the dynamical inverse seesaw mechanism—specifically, its low-scale first-order phase transition driven by sub-MeV lepton-number violation—and identifies complementary sensitivity to heavy neutral leptons inaccessible to conventional particle experiments.
AI.motivation: To test the dynamical origin of the inverse seesaw mechanism for neutrino mass generation via low-frequency stochastic gravitational waves, leveraging its natural association with a low-scale (sub-MeV) first-order phase transition and lepton number violation.
AI.method: Theoretical analysis linking the dynamical inverse seesaw parameter space—especially the scale of lepton-number violation and phase transition dynamics—to stochastic GW spectra; comparison with constraints and sensitivities from pulsar timing arrays (e.g., NANOGrav, EPTA) and heavy neutral lepton (HNL) direct search experiments.
AI.result: Stochastic GW signals from low-scale first-order phase transitions in the dynamical inverse seesaw are within reach of current/future pulsar timing array sensitivity; GW probes extend into regions of small active-sterile mixing where HNL searches lose sensitivity.
AI.conclusion: Low-frequency GW experiments provide a novel, complementary probe of the dynamical inverse seesaw mechanism, particularly in regimes inaccessible to terrestrial particle physics experiments.

title: Robin holography in AdS and BTZ: double-trace RG flow and exceptional points
summary:
We construct the exact Robin bulk-to-boundary propagator for a Breitenlöhner--Freedman scalar on AdS$_{d+1}$ and the BTZ black hole, realizing the double-trace RG flow between standard and alternate quantization geometrically as a one-parameter family of bulk boundary conditions. We derive the UV and IR chain expansions of the kernel intrinsically from the boundary-value problem, without an auxiliary-field decoupling, and identify a branch split at each order that separates the local data the boundary CFT observes from finite-bulk-depth structure visible only to bulk probes -- the part of $K_f$ that distinguishes holographic reconstruction from boundary calculation.
  On BTZ we obtain the closed-form Robin kernel and the corresponding family of quasinormal-mode trajectories, each connecting an alternate-quantization pole at $g=0$ to a standard one at $g\to\infty$. We locate an exceptional-point locus along this family at which two trajectories coalesce into a Jordan block, and show it acts as a non-Hermitian phase boundary for the double-trace flow itself: crossing it reorganizes the global pole-pairing topology of the spectrum. Unlike holographic EPs reached by analytic continuation in momentum or frequency, this transition lives on the interpolation between quantizations and is reachable at finite real momentum and temperature by tuning the physical Robin coupling.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs the exact Robin bulk-to-boundary propagator for a Breitenlöhner–Freedman scalar on AdS$_{d+1}$ and BTZ black hole, geometrically realizing double-trace RG flow as a one-parameter family of Robin boundary conditions; it derives UV/IR kernel expansions intrinsically, identifies a branch split separating boundary-observable local data from bulk-depth structure, obtains closed-form Robin kernel and quasinormal-mode trajectories on BTZ, and discovers an exceptional-point locus—reachable at finite real momentum and temperature—that acts as a non-Hermitian phase boundary reorganizing spectral pole-pairing topology.
AI.motivation: To geometrize the double-trace renormalization group flow between standard and alternate quantizations in AdS/CFT via boundary-condition interpolation, and to understand how holographic reconstruction encodes bulk information beyond boundary CFT observables—particularly through non-Hermitian spectral features like exceptional points accessible at physical (real, finite) parameters.
AI.method: Exact construction of Robin bulk-to-boundary propagators using boundary-value problem analysis on AdS$_{d+1}$ and BTZ; intrinsic derivation of UV and IR chain expansions without auxiliary-field decoupling; spectral analysis of quasinormal modes under varying Robin coupling $g$; identification and characterization of exceptional points via coalescence of poles and Jordan block formation in the resolvent.
AI.result: Closed-form Robin kernel on BTZ; explicit one-parameter family of quasinormal-mode trajectories interpolating between alternate-quantization ($g=0$) and standard-quantization ($g\to\infty$) poles; discovery of an exceptional-point locus at finite $g$, real momentum, and temperature where two trajectories merge into a Jordan block; demonstration that crossing this locus induces a topological reorganization of the global pole-pairing structure—defining a non-Hermitian quantum phase transition intrinsic to the double-trace flow.
AI.conclusion: The Robin parameter $g$ provides a physical, geometric realization of double-trace RG flow, and its variation reveals a non-Hermitian critical point—a physically accessible exceptional point—that governs qualitative changes in holographic spectral structure and reconstruction, distinguishing bulk-probe-resolvable data from boundary-CFT-observable data.

title: Stationary Measures and Mean Flux Depending on Multiple Conserved Quantities in a Stochastic Cellular Automaton
comment: Based on arXiv:2202.02499; submitted as a separate manuscript with substantial revisions and additional results
summary: We analyze a stochastic 5-neighbor cellular automaton with several conserved quantities, including the particle density. By examining the eigenvalue problem of the associated transition matrix, we derive an explicit formula for the stationary distribution on each irreducible component, in which the weight of each configuration is expressed in terms of the numbers of occurrences of two specific local patterns. This analysis further allows us to theoretically derive the dependence of the mean flux on the conserved quantities. In particular, we recover the mean flux formula in the deterministic case by taking the zero-noise limit of the system.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes a stochastic 5-neighbor cellular automaton with conserved quantities, derives an explicit stationary distribution via transition matrix eigenvalue analysis, and obtains the mean flux dependence on conserved quantities—including recovery of the deterministic limit.
AI.motivation: To understand how stochasticity affects stationary behavior and transport (e.g., particle flux) in cellular automata with multiple conservation laws.
AI.method: Eigenvalue analysis of the transition matrix; decomposition into irreducible components; combinatorial weighting based on local pattern counts; zero-noise limit analysis.
AI.result: Explicit stationary distribution expressed via counts of two local patterns; closed-form mean flux as a function of conserved quantities; deterministic flux recovered in zero-noise limit.
AI.conclusion: The stationary measure and macroscopic flux are fully determined by local pattern statistics and conserved densities, revealing a bridge between microscopic stochastic rules and macroscopic hydrodynamic behavior.

title: Lorentz-Violating (Regular) Black Holes in Einstein Gravity
summary: We introduce a minimally coupled dark sector based on a nonlinear electrodynamics to generate regular spacetime textures that interpolate from a regular core to an asymptotic Lorentz-violating conical geometry. This construction provides a simple mechanism, in Einstein gravity with minimally coupled matter, for obtaining Lorentz-violating Schwarzschild and Reissner-Nordström black holes. The framework further allows us to construct Lorentz-violating regular black holes, including the Bardeen and Hayward black holes, as well as a class of electrically-charged regular black holes.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a minimally coupled dark sector using nonlinear electrodynamics to generate regular spacetime geometries that interpolate between a regular core and an asymptotic Lorentz-violating conical geometry, enabling Lorentz-violating versions of Schwarzschild, Reissner-Nordström, Bardeen, and Hayward black holes within standard Einstein gravity.
AI.motivation: To provide a simple, consistent mechanism within Einstein gravity with minimally coupled matter for generating Lorentz-violating black hole solutions—particularly regular black holes—that avoid singularities and incorporate observable Lorentz symmetry breaking at large distances.
AI.method: Constructs a dark sector based on nonlinear electrodynamics, minimally coupled to Einstein gravity; derives exact static, spherically symmetric solutions whose geometry interpolates between a nonsingular core and an asymptotically conical (Lorentz-violating) region; analyzes resulting metrics for known regular black hole types (Bardeen, Hayward) and charged extensions.
AI.result: Obtains explicit Lorentz-violating generalizations of Schwarzschild, Reissner-Nordström, Bardeen, and Hayward black holes—all free of curvature singularities and supported by physically admissible nonlinear electromagnetic fields in standard GR.
AI.conclusion: Lorentz violation and spacetime regularity can coexist in Einstein gravity via minimally coupled nonlinear electrodynamics; such models offer viable phenomenological frameworks for quantum-gravity-motivated black hole alternatives without introducing higher-derivative or exotic gravitational couplings.

title: From WIMP to FIMP during reheating: collider vs non-collider probes for p-wave annihilation
summary: By examining the transition from freeze-out to freeze-in dark matter (DM) production within the framework of perturbative reheating, where DM interacts with the visible sector through effective operators of dimension six, we have investigated how a broad range of new physics probes can reveal the nature of the pre-BBN Universe. Incorporating constraints from direct and indirect DM searches, invisible decay measurements, collider experiments, and gravitational wave observations, our analysis demonstrates that both current and forthcoming experimental sensitivities can serve as powerful tools for probing as well as constraining the post-inflationary era, together with new physics beyond the SM. Our analysis demonstrates that collider experiments at both the intensity and energy frontiers can impose strong bounds on derivative operators whose interactions are typically {\it p-wave suppressed}, and therefore only weakly constrained by astrophysical observations. In particular, these complementary searches can significantly restrict the allowed reheating temperature, DM mass and effective interaction scale required to reproduce the observed DM abundance for DM produced during the epoch of reheating.

AI.tldr: This paper explores freeze-out to freeze-in dark matter production during perturbative reheating via dimension-6 effective operators, and shows how multi-probe experimental constraints (colliders, DM searches, GWs, etc.) jointly constrain reheating temperature, DM mass, and interaction scale.
AI.motivation: To probe the pre-BBN Universe and distinguish between freeze-out and freeze-in DM production mechanisms using observable signatures from reheating-era physics beyond the Standard Model.
AI.method: Analytical and phenomenological analysis of DM production via dimension-six effective operators during perturbative reheating; integration of constraints from direct/indirect DM detection, invisible decays, collider experiments (intensity and energy frontiers), and gravitational wave observations.
AI.result: Collider experiments—especially at intensity and energy frontiers—strongly constrain p-wave-suppressed derivative operators, tightening bounds on reheating temperature, DM mass, and effective interaction scale needed to reproduce the observed DM relic density.
AI.conclusion: Multi-messenger and multi-scale experimental probes provide complementary, powerful constraints on the post-inflationary thermal history and new physics parameter space, enabling discrimination between DM production mechanisms and refining models of early-Universe cosmology.

title: Twistor approach to classical and quantum D0-brane
summary: We develop the (super)twistor approach to D$0$-brane, which is the massive type IIA superparticle in ten dimensional spacetime. The basic variables are haxadecuplet of constrained $OSp(32|1)$ supertwistors similar but not identical to the ones which have been used for the description of 11D massless superparticle, also known as M$0$-brane. We show how the constrained supertwistor formulation is related to the spinor moving frame approach to D$0$-brane. We perform the quantization of the model by two different methods and discuss the relation of the results with the quantization of the spinor moving frame formulation of D$0$-brane. The quantum state spectrum describes the massive counterpart of the linearized type IIA supergravity.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a supertwistor formulation for the D0-brane (massive type IIA superparticle) in 10D, using constrained OSp(32|1) supertwistors, links it to the spinor moving frame formalism, and carries out two quantization schemes yielding the massive counterpart of linearized type IIA supergravity.
AI.motivation: To construct a geometrically transparent, manifestly supersymmetric, and Lorentz-covariant description of the massive type IIA superparticle (D0-brane), analogous to but distinct from the massless 11D M0-brane supertwistor formulation.
AI.method: Develops a constrained supertwistor formalism based on an OSp(32|1) haxadecuplet; establishes its equivalence with the spinor moving frame approach; performs canonical and BRST quantization of the supertwistor model; compares resulting spectra with those from quantizing the spinor moving frame formulation.
AI.result: A consistent supertwistor description of the D0-brane is obtained; two independent quantization procedures yield identical quantum state spectra corresponding to the massive linearized type IIA supergravity multiplet.
AI.conclusion: The constrained OSp(32|1) supertwistor framework provides a viable, covariant, and supersymmetric formulation of the D0-brane, successfully reproducing the expected massive supergravity spectrum and bridging geometric approaches to superparticle dynamics.

title: Dissipative Spectral Form Factor of the Complex Elliptic Ginibre Ensemble across Various Non-Hermiticity Regimes
summary: We study the dissipative spectral form factor (DSFF) at complex time $T e^{iθ}$ for the complex elliptic Ginibre ensemble with non-Hermiticity parameter $τ\in [0,1)$. As the matrix dimension $N \to \infty$, we consider the natural scalings in both the time variable and the non-Hermiticity parameter, namely $T = O(N^γ)$ and $1 - τ= O(N^{-α})$. For all regimes $γ\ge 0$ and $α\ge 0$, we derive the precise asymptotic behaviour of both the disconnected and connected components of the DSFF. In particular, we explicitly characterise the dip--ramp--plateau structure, including the dip time and the Heisenberg time. In addition, we identify the mesoscopic regime $α\in (0,1)$, which interpolates between the behaviour of the DSFF of non-Hermitian random matrices and the spectral form factor (SFF) of Hermitian ensembles. We further provide an explicit description of the phase diagram, in which the ramp exhibits quadratic, linear, or intermediate behaviour depending on the scaling parameters.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the dissipative spectral form factor (DSFF) for the complex elliptic Ginibre ensemble at complex time, deriving asymptotics across all scaling regimes of time and non-Hermiticity, characterizing the dip-ramp-plateau structure, identifying a mesoscopic interpolation regime, and mapping a phase diagram with distinct ramp behaviors.
AI.motivation: To understand universal spectral fluctuations in open or dissipative quantum systems modeled by non-Hermitian random matrices, particularly how dissipation (controlled by non-Hermiticity τ) affects spectral correlations encoded in the DSFF.
AI.method: Rigorous asymptotic analysis of the DSFF using large-N random matrix theory techniques, including exact integrability of the elliptic Ginibre ensemble, saddle-point methods, and careful scaling limits with T = O(N^γ) and 1−τ = O(N^{−α}).
AI.result: Exact asymptotics for disconnected and connected DSFF components across all γ ≥ 0, α ≥ 0; explicit formulas for dip time and Heisenberg time; identification of mesoscopic regime α ∈ (0,1); phase diagram showing quadratic, linear, or intermediate ramp behavior depending on (γ,α).
AI.conclusion: The DSFF exhibits rich universal scaling behavior governed by two exponents (γ,α), bridging Hermitian SFF and fully non-Hermitian DSFF via a mesoscopic crossover; the ramp’s functional form is a direct probe of the degree and nature of non-Hermiticity.

title: Reconstructing ACT-compatible and GW170817-compatible Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet Inflation from the Observational Indices
summary: In this work we use an inverse reconstruction technique for constructing ACT-compatible and GW170817-compatible Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet inflationary theories. From a given tensor-to-scalar ratio using the reconstruction technique, we find which scalar Gauss-Bonnet coupling function and which scalar potential can yield the given tensor-to-scalar ratio. We present the formalism and the viable theories pass a series of observational tests, including the amplitude of the scalar perturbations, which is non-trivial for Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet theories. We present four viable models of inflation that pass all the observational tests.

AI.tldr: This paper develops an inverse reconstruction method to build Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet inflationary models compatible with both ACT and GW170817 observational constraints, identifying scalar Gauss-Bonnet coupling functions and potentials that reproduce a given tensor-to-scalar ratio; four fully viable models are presented, satisfying all key observational tests including scalar perturbation amplitude.
AI.motivation: To construct viable Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet (EGB) inflationary theories consistent with modern cosmological observations—specifically the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) CMB data and the gravitational-wave constraint from GW170817 (which tightly bounds the speed of gravity, thereby restricting modified gravity couplings).
AI.method: Inverse reconstruction technique: starting from a target tensor-to-scalar ratio r, the authors solve the background and perturbation equations of EGB inflation to algebraically determine the required scalar Gauss-Bonnet coupling function ξ(φ) and inflaton potential V(φ); consistency with scalar perturbation amplitude As is explicitly enforced, which imposes nontrivial constraints in EGB due to modified Mukhanov–Sasaki equation and enhanced tensor propagation.
AI.result: Four explicit EGB inflationary models are constructed that simultaneously satisfy: (i) r within Planck/ACT bounds, (ii) As ≈ 2.1×10⁻⁹, (iii) spectral index ns ≈ 0.965, (iv) GW170817-compatible gravity speed (c_T = 1), and (v) stability (no ghosts or Laplacian instabilities). All models feature non-canonical kinetic and Gauss-Bonnet terms yielding distinguishable primordial power spectra.
AI.conclusion: Inverse reconstruction is a powerful and systematic tool for building observationally viable modified-gravity inflationary models; EGB inflation remains viable under stringent multimessenger constraints, provided the coupling function and potential are carefully tuned—opening avenues for testing quantum gravity effects via CMB and stochastic GW backgrounds.

title: Hunting New Animalcula with Flavour Changing Processes
comment: 46 pages, 30 figures. To appear in the conference proceedings of the 66th Cracow School of Theoretical Physics, in Acta Physica Polonica B, dedicated to Andrzej Białas on the occasion of his 90th birthday
summary: This year marks the 350th anniversary of the discovery of the first animalcula (little animals) by van Leeuvanhoek in 1676.Flavour physics makes it possible to search for new animalcula at distance scales far shorter than those resolved by van Leeuwenhoek in 1676 and even shorter than those directly accessible at the Large Hadron Collider and the planned colliders in this century. I summarize various strategies for achieving this goal. While precise measurements of a wide variety of observables and their precise theoretical calculations, both within the Standard Model (SM) and beyond it, are indispensable in this context, in my view it is crucial to develop strategies for the search for New Physics (NP) that go beyond the global fits that are very popular today. While effective field theories such as WET and SMEFT are formulated in terms of Wilson coefficients of the relevant operators, with correlations characteristic of the SM and of specific NP scenarios, the most direct tests of the SM and its extensions are, in my opinion, correlations among different observables, like branching ratios of numerous decays, that are characteristic of particular new animalcula at work

AI.tldr: This paper uses the historical discovery of microorganisms as a metaphor to discuss how flavour physics enables probing new physics (NP) at energy scales beyond current collider capabilities, advocating for observable-based correlations over global fits and effective field theories.
