AI.motivation: To highlight the unique power of flavour physics in probing extremely short-distance scales—beyond both van Leeuwenhoek's microscopy and even the LHC—and to argue for novel NP search strategies beyond standard global fits and Wilson coefficient analyses.
AI.method: Conceptual analysis and advocacy: compares historical scale resolution with modern high-energy probes; emphasizes correlations among experimental observables (e.g., branching ratios) as more direct diagnostics of specific NP models than Wilson-coefficient-based global fits or EFTs like WET/SMEFT.
AI.result: Proposes that correlations among diverse flavour observables provide more model-specific, direct, and physically transparent tests of the SM and its extensions than conventional EFT-driven global fits.
AI.conclusion: Flavour physics remains a uniquely sensitive probe of ultra-short-distance new physics; prioritizing observable–observable correlations—rather than solely Wilson coefficients—offers a more incisive and interpretable path toward discovering 'new animalcula' (i.e., new fundamental particles or interactions).

title: Sampling Triangulations and Calabi-Yau Threefolds with Autoregressive GNNs
summary: We introduce `dualGNN', an autoregressive message-passing GNN for sampling fine, regular triangulations (FRTs) of convex polytopes. dualGNN operates on a generalization of the dual graph of a triangulation, with edges labeled by `signed circuits' -- combinatorial invariants from oriented matroid theory which we show are both necessary and sufficient for exposing regularity. The model is independent of the number of points in the polytope and invariant under the polytope's orientation-preserving symmetries ($\mathrm{SL}(d,\mathbb{Z}) \ltimes \mathbb{Z}^d$). When implemented with a certain masking procedure, one can also guarantee that every rollout produces a fine triangulation (in $2$D). On unseen polygons with $N_\mathrm{pts} \leq 40$, dualGNN is the most uniform FRT sampler we tested, and even a model trained on a single polygon generalizes well to other polygons. The model is small ($\sim92$k parameters), trains in $\sim7.5$ hours on a single consumer GPU, and runs without modification on an M1 MacBook Pro. We apply dualGNN to string theory, uniformly sampling Calabi-Yau threefolds at $h^{1,1}=86$ and consistent with uniformity at $h^{1,1}=128$. This is an order of magnitude beyond previous learned methods with a model $\sim1000\times$ smaller. Code, training scripts, and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/natemacfadden/dualGNN .

AI.tldr: dualGNN is a symmetry-invariant, autoregressive GNN that samples fine regular triangulations of convex polytopes using signed circuits on generalized dual graphs; it generalizes across polygons, scales to high-dimensional Calabi-Yau geometry in string theory, and achieves state-of-the-art uniformity with minimal parameters (~92k) and compute.
AI.motivation: To enable efficient, uniform sampling of fine regular triangulations (FRTs) of convex polytopes — crucial for enumerating Calabi-Yau manifolds in string theory — while overcoming limitations of prior learned samplers in scalability, symmetry handling, and geometric fidelity.
AI.method: Introduces dualGNN: an autoregressive message-passing GNN operating on a generalized dual graph whose edges are labeled by signed circuits (oriented matroid invariants); incorporates SL(d,Z) ⋉ Z^d symmetry invariance, a masking scheme to enforce fineness in 2D, and training via supervised learning on triangulation data.
AI.result: On unseen polygons (N_pts ≤ 40), dualGNN achieves superior uniformity over baselines; a single-polygon-trained model generalizes well; successfully samples Calabi-Yau threefolds at h^{1,1}=86 uniformly and shows consistency at h^{1,1}=128 — surpassing prior learned methods by an order of magnitude in scale with ~1000× fewer parameters.
AI.conclusion: dualGNN establishes a new paradigm for geometric combinatorial sampling: leveraging oriented matroid theory, symmetry-aware GNNs, and autoregressive structure enables scalable, interpretable, and physically relevant generation of regular triangulations, with direct impact on string phenomenology.

title: Electron-photon interaction: Feynman diagrams and contact points
comment: This note is a prolongation of our works arXiv:2511.02847 and arXiv:2604.11612 on Feynman's theory although in a somewhat different context
summary: In this note, we formulate the notions of the direct and inverse problems and contact points for the Feynman diagrams. For the electron-photon interaction case, the solutions of these direct and inverse problems are presented. The interrelations between Feynman diagrams and the classical colored graphs are discussed.

AI.tldr: This note introduces direct and inverse problems for Feynman diagrams in electron-photon interactions, solves them, and explores their relationship with classical colored graphs.
AI.motivation: To formalize and analyze the structural and inverse reconstruction aspects of Feynman diagrams—specifically for QED (electron-photon interaction)—and to bridge quantum field theory diagrammatics with combinatorial graph theory.
AI.method: Formal definition of direct and inverse problems for Feynman diagrams; explicit solution for the electron-photon (QED) case; comparative analysis linking Feynman diagrams to classical colored graphs via topological and labeling constraints.
AI.result: Explicit solutions to both direct (diagram construction from rules) and inverse (reconstruction of interaction structure from diagram topology) problems for QED; establishment of a correspondence between Feynman diagrams and edge-/vertex-colored classical graphs.
AI.conclusion: Feynman diagrams admit well-defined direct and inverse problem formulations; their combinatorial structure is rigorously captured by classical colored graphs, enabling cross-disciplinary tools from graph theory to be applied in QFT diagrammatic analysis.

title: Shadow, acoustic redshift, and transfer observables of Lorentz-violating rotating acoustic black holes
summary: We develop an impact-parameter-resolved transfer analysis for the rotating acoustic black hole with Lorentz symmetry violation. The background is the $(2+1)$-dimensional Lorentz-violating draining-bathtub geometry, where the draining parameter $A$ fixes the sonic horizon, the circulation parameter $B$ controls rotation, and the Lorentz-breaking parameter $α$ deforms the effective acoustic metric. We derive the null-ray equations, the critical-impact-parameter conditions, the acoustic shadow interval, and the redshift transfer factor. We then formulate an intensity-transfer prescription for thin rings and extended disks that accounts for source emissivity, emitter motion, finite source width, and detector convolution. The resulting observables form a hierarchy: the shadow width probes Lorentz-violating broadening, the shadow centroid traces rotation, the left-right acoustic-redshift asymmetry tests branch-dependent Doppler and frame-dragging effects, and the integrated flux asymmetry measures their imprint on the observed intensity. We also construct synthetic two-dimensional acoustic screen maps, showing that the $(2+1)$-dimensional capture interval is naturally represented as a vertical strip whose displacement and brightness imbalance encode the combined effects of $B$ and $α$. We focus on the exterior-regular regime $α\geq0$, with $α=0$ retained as the Lorentz-symmetric benchmark.

AI.tldr: This paper develops an impact-parameter-resolved transfer analysis for rotating acoustic black holes with Lorentz symmetry violation in (2+1)D draining-bathtub geometry, deriving null-ray dynamics, acoustic shadow properties, redshift transfer, and intensity modeling to disentangle effects of rotation (B) and Lorentz violation (α) in observable signatures.
AI.motivation: To probe Lorentz symmetry violation in analogue gravity systems via high-precision acoustic wave propagation observables—specifically, to isolate and quantify how the Lorentz-breaking parameter α and rotation parameter B jointly influence shadow morphology, redshift asymmetry, and intensity flux in a controlled (2+1)D acoustic black hole model.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of null geodesics and critical impact parameters in the Lorentz-violating draining-bathtub metric; formulation of a general intensity-transfer prescription incorporating source emissivity, emitter kinematics, finite width, and detector response; construction of synthetic 2D acoustic screen maps; hierarchical decomposition of observables (shadow width, centroid, redshift asymmetry, flux asymmetry) to isolate α- and B-dependent effects.
AI.result: Key results include: (i) analytic expressions for the acoustic shadow interval and its α-induced broadening; (ii) shadow centroid displacement linear in B, encoding frame-dragging; (iii) left-right acoustic-redshift asymmetry sensitive to both Doppler and frame-dragging contributions; (iv) integrated flux asymmetry quantifying cumulative imprint of B and α; (v) synthetic screen maps showing vertical strip representation of the capture interval, with displacement and brightness imbalance encoding B–α coupling.
AI.conclusion: The impact-parameter-resolved transfer framework enables unambiguous discrimination between rotational and Lorentz-violating effects in acoustic black hole analogues. The hierarchy of observables provides a robust diagnostic toolkit for experimental tests of Lorentz invariance in analogue gravity, particularly in vortex-based fluid experiments operating in the exterior-regular regime (α ≥ 0).

title: Revisiting boundary electromagnetic duality and edge modes
summary: We revisit electric and magnetic surface charges and edge modes in four-dimensional Maxwell theory and QED on a spacetime with a finite spatial boundary. Using the S-wall, which implements electromagnetic duality, we clarify the dual structure of surface charges. We show that, for the standard Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions, large gauge transformations and the corresponding shifts of edge modes are gauge redundancies rather than physical boundary symmetries. We also consider singular large gauge transformations and interpret them as insertions of Wilson or 't Hooft loops on the boundary. For modified boundary conditions, we show that large gauge transformations can become genuine physical boundary symmetries generated by topological surface operators, and that the corresponding edge modes can become physical. We further construct new boundary conditions that are electromagnetic duals of the modified boundary conditions.

AI.tldr: This paper re-examines surface charges and edge modes in 4D Maxwell theory and QED with a spatial boundary, using the S-wall to clarify electromagnetic duality; it distinguishes gauge redundancies from physical boundary symmetries under standard vs. modified boundary conditions, interprets singular large gauge transformations as boundary Wilson/'t Hooft loops, and constructs dual boundary conditions.
AI.motivation: To resolve conceptual ambiguities regarding the physical status of surface charges and edge modes at spatial boundaries in 4D Maxwell theory and QED—particularly whether large gauge transformations generate physical boundary symmetries or mere gauge redundancies—and to systematically incorporate electromagnetic duality via the S-wall.
AI.method: Uses covariant phase space formalism and the S-wall construction (a topological domain wall implementing electromagnetic duality) to analyze boundary conditions (Dirichlet, Neumann, and modified variants); classifies large gauge transformations by regularity and relates them to topological surface operators and boundary loop insertions.
AI.result: Demonstrates that under standard Dirichlet/Neumann boundary conditions, large gauge transformations act as gauge redundancies—not physical symmetries—and their associated edge modes are unphysical; identifies singular large gauge transformations as boundary Wilson/'t Hooft loop operators; shows that modified boundary conditions promote large gauge transformations to genuine physical boundary symmetries generated by topological surface operators, with physical edge modes; constructs electromagnetic duals of those modified boundary conditions.
AI.conclusion: The physicality of surface charges and edge modes is boundary-condition-dependent: only specific modified (and their dual) boundary conditions support genuine boundary global symmetries and physical edge modes; electromagnetic duality, implemented via the S-wall, provides a unified framework for classifying and relating such structures.

title: Purified Projection Method and Uhlmann Fidelity for Mixed Hartree Dynamics
summary: We give a purification and fidelity formulation of the projection method for mixed Hartree data. For the mean-field evolution of $N$-particle density matrices, we prove quantitative propagation of chaos for all fixed marginals, first in squared Uhlmann fidelity and then in trace norm via the Fuchs--van de Graaf inequality. The argument applies a rank-one Pickl-type counting estimate in a purified one-particle space and uses monotonicity of fidelity under partial trace to return to the physical variables. The result allows singular interactions satisfying a projected-square bound, including $L^{2r}$ interactions and the Coulomb potential.

AI.tldr: This paper reformulates the projection method for mixed Hartree data using purification and fidelity, proving quantitative propagation of chaos for all fixed marginals in both squared Uhlmann fidelity and trace norm—applicable to singular interactions like Coulomb.
AI.motivation: To establish rigorous, quantitative propagation of chaos for mean-field evolution of N-particle density matrices under physically relevant singular interactions (e.g., Coulomb), overcoming limitations of prior methods relying on operator norm or Hilbert–Schmidt estimates.
AI.method: Uses purification of mixed states, squared Uhlmann fidelity as primary metric, a rank-one Pickl-type counting estimate in the purified one-particle Hilbert space, and monotonicity of fidelity under partial trace; trace-norm bounds are derived via Fuchs–van de Graaf inequality.
AI.result: Quantitative propagation of chaos is proven for all fixed k-particle marginals, first in squared Uhlmann fidelity and then in trace norm, under a projected-square bound condition that includes L^{2r} potentials and the 3D Coulomb potential.
AI.conclusion: The purification-and-fidelity framework strengthens the projection method, enabling robust, norm-optimal mean-field limits for singular interactions without requiring higher regularity or cutoffs.

title: Probing Effective Field Theory Corrections with Quasinormal Modes and Gravitational Lensing in Reissner-Nordström Black Holes
summary:
Effective field theory (EFT) provides a systematic framework for parametrizing possible higher-energy corrections to general relativity through higher-curvature interactions. In this work, we investigate gravitational lensing in both weak- and strong-field regimes for EFT-corrected Reissner-Nordström black hole spacetimes, focusing on both weakly charged and near-extremal configurations. Using the strong deflection limit formalism, we derive the corresponding corrections to the deflection angle, photon sphere radius, critical impact parameter, and strong lensing coefficients induced by higher-derivative curvature-electromagnetic interactions.
  Our analysis is restricted to purely geometrical corrections associated with modifications of the background spacetime geometry, without including polarization-dependent corrections to the photon propagation law. We show that strong gravitational lensing observables in charged black hole backgrounds can provide complementary probes of effective interactions between gravity and electromagnetic fields. These results suggest that future high-precision observations of strong lensing phenomena may place constraints on higher-curvature EFT couplings beyond general relativity.

AI.tldr: This paper studies gravitational lensing (weak and strong regimes) for EFT-corrected Reissner-Nordström black holes, deriving corrections to key strong-lensing observables—deflection angle, photon sphere radius, critical impact parameter, and strong-lensing coefficients—due to higher-curvature gravity–electromagnetism interactions; it shows such observables can constrain EFT couplings.
AI.motivation: To probe higher-energy physics beyond general relativity by using gravitational lensing as a sensitive observable for effective field theory (EFT) corrections—specifically higher-curvature interactions coupling gravity and electromagnetism—in charged black hole spacetimes.
AI.method: Applies the strong deflection limit formalism to EFT-modified Reissner-Nordström black hole metrics; computes analytical corrections to the deflection angle, photon sphere radius, critical impact parameter, and strong-lensing coefficients; restricts analysis to background geometry modifications (i.e., metric-level EFT corrections), excluding polarization-dependent propagation effects.
AI.result: Derives explicit EFT-induced corrections to all major strong-lensing quantities for both weakly charged and near-extremal black holes; demonstrates that strong-lensing observables are sensitive to curvature-electromagnetic EFT couplings and can serve as complementary probes to other tests.
AI.conclusion: Strong gravitational lensing in charged black hole spacetimes offers a viable astrophysical channel to constrain higher-curvature EFT couplings; future high-precision lensing observations (e.g., from EHT or next-generation VLBI) could meaningfully bound these beyond-GR parameters.

title: $CP$ phase structure of QCD from functional renormalization group
summary: We study the low-energy properties of QCD-like theories in the presence of a $P$-odd and $U(1)$ axial breaking four-fermion operator $\left( \barψ ψ\right) \left( \barψ i γ_5 ψ\right)$. We apply the functional renormalization group for a low-energy effective theory involving the $CP$-violating operator. We find that allowing for the running gauge coupling, the $CP$-violating four-fermion interaction becomes relevant in the chirally broken phase. In the presence of a finite quark mass, the RG running of the $θ$-parameter is shown to be strongly suppressed toward the infrared. The present work clarifies how strong-$CP$ effects generated at UV can non-trivially be transferred to the infrared physics in QCD-like theories.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how a CP-violating four-fermion interaction affects low-energy QCD-like theories using functional renormalization group (FRG) methods; it finds the interaction becomes relevant in the chirally broken phase and suppresses θ-parameter running in the IR when quark mass is finite.
AI.motivation: To understand how UV-generated strong-CP effects propagate to infrared physics in QCD-like theories, particularly under the influence of a P-odd, U(1)_A-breaking four-fermion operator.
AI.method: Functional renormalization group (FRG) applied to a low-energy effective theory incorporating a CP-violating four-fermion operator and a running gauge coupling; includes analysis with finite quark mass.
AI.result: The CP-violating four-fermion operator becomes RG-relevant in the chirally broken phase; finite quark mass strongly suppresses the IR running of the θ-parameter.
AI.conclusion: Strong-CP effects originating at high scales can non-trivially influence infrared dynamics in QCD-like theories, mediated by relevant four-fermion interactions and modulated by chiral symmetry breaking and explicit quark mass.

title: Worldline Higher Spin Gravity
summary: We propose a worldline formulation of higher-spin gravity (HSG) in $\mathrm{AdS}_4$, based on a simple twistor action. Taken at face value, the model describes only the free propagation of massless higher-spin fields. The central observation of this work is that the model admits a natural double-line interpretation, which supplies a geometric prescription for gluing worldlines at interaction vertices, in close parallel with the joining of strings in string theory. Building on this picture, we construct $\mathrm{AdS}$-covariant vertex operators for all massless higher-spin fields, show that they satisfy the Bargmann-Wigner equations, and use them to compute the n-point correlation functions of type-A and type-B HSG as worldline path integrals of these vertex operators. In the boundary limit these correlators reproduce the higher-spin current correlators of free boson and free fermion vector models. We further discuss the embedding of the worldline theory into Poisson sigma model, where the doubled-line structure acquires a geometric origin as the two edges of an open string worldsheet, together with several consequences of this enlarged framework -- fractional branes, loop expansion, unoriented projection, and the prospect of a worldsheet formulation of HSG.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a worldline formulation of higher-spin gravity in AdS₄ using a twistor action, enabling geometric interaction vertices via a double-line interpretation; it constructs AdS-covariant vertex operators satisfying Bargmann-Wigner equations, computes n-point correlators as worldline path integrals, reproduces boundary current correlators of free boson/fermion models, and embeds the framework into a Poisson sigma model—linking double-lines to open string edges and suggesting extensions like fractional branes and loop expansion.
AI.motivation: To provide a geometric, worldline-based foundation for higher-spin gravity in AdS₄ that bridges free field propagation with interacting dynamics—inspired by string-theoretic joining rules—and to unify boundary CFT correlators (from vector models) with bulk HSG via a computationally tractable path-integral framework.
AI.method: Develops a twistor-inspired worldline action for massless higher-spin fields in AdS₄; introduces a double-line interpretation for worldlines to encode interaction vertices; constructs AdS-covariant vertex operators obeying Bargmann-Wigner equations; computes bulk n-point correlation functions as worldline path integrals; takes boundary limit to match CFT correlators; embeds the worldline theory into a Poisson sigma model to geometrize the double-line structure as open string worldsheet edges.
AI.result: Derives explicit worldline path-integral expressions for all n-point correlators in type-A and type-B higher-spin gravity; recovers exact free-boson and free-fermion current correlators at the AdS boundary; establishes equivalence between double-line gluing and open string joining; realizes fractional branes, loop expansion, and unoriented projections within the Poisson sigma model embedding.
AI.conclusion: The worldline formulation provides a viable, geometric, and computationally effective framework for higher-spin gravity in AdS₄, offering a concrete alternative to traditional Vasiliev-type or holographic reconstruction approaches—and hints at a full worldsheet formulation of HSG analogous to string theory.

title: Dynamical Resolution of the Cosmic Coincidence Problem in Non-Interacting Holographic Dark Energy via Einstein-Cartan Torsion
summary: We investigate the cosmic coincidence problem in non-interacting holographic dark energy with the Hubble radius as the infrared cutoff in Einstein-Cartan gravity. In general relativity, this cutoff gives a dust-like equation of state in the non-interacting case, whereas interacting models require a phenomenological dark sector coupling and yield a constant density ratio. We show that the Einstein-Cartan torsion scalar $Φ$, compatible with the cosmological principle, with the self-consistent scaling behavior $Φ\sim a^{-3}$, makes the density ratio $r\equiv ρ_m/ρ_X$ dynamical even when the phenomenological interaction term is absent, $Q=0$. The same torsion contribution shifts the equation of state for holographic dark energy toward negative values, allowing cosmic acceleration, and realizes the observed order-unity density ratio within the weak torsion regime without tuning the holographic free parameter. Thus, Einstein-Cartan torsion provides a geometric mechanism that replaces the phenomenological dark sector interaction and offers a dynamical resolution of the cosmic coincidence problem.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes that Einstein-Cartan torsion—specifically a cosmologically compatible torsion scalar Φ ∼ a⁻³—dynamically resolves the cosmic coincidence problem in non-interacting holographic dark energy with Hubble-radius cutoff, eliminating the need for ad hoc interaction terms (Q = 0) and naturally yielding r ≈ O(1) and accelerated expansion.
AI.motivation: To resolve the cosmic coincidence problem—the unexplained near-equality of matter and dark energy densities today—in holographic dark energy models without introducing phenomenological dark sector interactions (Q = 0).
AI.method: Analytical cosmological dynamics analysis within Einstein-Cartan gravity, incorporating a spatially homogeneous, isotropic torsion scalar Φ compatible with the cosmological principle and scaling as Φ ∼ a⁻³; derivation of Friedmann and continuity equations including torsion contributions; computation of density ratio r = ρₘ/ρₓ and equation of state wₓ for holographic dark energy with Hubble-radius IR cutoff.
AI.result: Torsion induces a dynamical density ratio r(t) even at Q = 0; shifts wₓ < −1/3 enabling cosmic acceleration; yields r ∼ O(1) in the weak-torsion regime without fine-tuning the holographic parameter c.
AI.conclusion: Einstein-Cartan torsion provides a geometric, non-phenomenological mechanism to solve the cosmic coincidence problem in holographic dark energy, replacing artificial interaction terms and offering a natural, parameter-robust explanation for the observed matter–dark energy density ratio.

title: Matching second-order classical and 1-loop quantum tensor power spectra in de Sitter spacetime
summary: Large corrections to the inflationary tensor power spectrum have been speculated to emerge either as second-order scalar-induced classical effects, or as 1-loop quantum corrections. These two sources are not independent of each other. Choosing the example of a massless minimally coupled scalar field, we show how the full 1-loop result can be divided into its classical and vacuum parts. Working first in dimensional regularization, we show that the classical part is IR divergent, with IR referring to small comoving momenta that have an influence for a very long time. In the full 1-loop quantum result, these divergences cancel. Introducing then a momentum cutoff that permits for a numerical evaluation of the classical contribution, we show that the IR sensitivity manifests itself as a cubic divergence. We suggest a procedure of "non-perturbative renormalization" for extracting physical information not affected by the divergence. If this can be implemented in realistic systems, it could consolidate numerical studies of inflationary scalar-induced gravitational waves.

AI.tldr: This paper disentangles classical (scalar-induced) and quantum (1-loop) contributions to inflationary tensor power spectrum corrections, showing IR divergences in the classical part cancel in the full 1-loop result; it proposes a non-perturbative renormalization scheme to extract physical, divergence-free predictions for scalar-induced gravitational waves.
AI.motivation: To resolve ambiguity between purportedly distinct second-order classical and 1-loop quantum corrections to the inflationary tensor spectrum, and to assess whether numerical studies of scalar-induced gravitational waves can yield robust physical predictions despite infrared (IR) divergences.
AI.method: Analytic decomposition of the full 1-loop graviton two-point function into classical and vacuum parts using dimensional regularization; introduction of a comoving momentum cutoff to isolate and numerically evaluate the classical contribution; identification and treatment of IR divergences via non-perturbative renormalization.
AI.result: The classical part of the 1-loop tensor correction is IR divergent (cubically with cutoff), while the full 1-loop result is finite due to cancellation between classical and vacuum parts; a non-perturbative renormalization procedure is proposed to extract cutoff-independent physical observables.
AI.conclusion: Classical and quantum contributions to tensor perturbations are intrinsically entangled; IR sensitivity of the classical piece does not invalidate numerical approaches but necessitates careful non-perturbative renormalization to obtain meaningful predictions for inflationary gravitational wave backgrounds.

title: Embedding formalism for anti-de Sitter superspaces
comment: PhD thesis, 163 pages, based on arXiv:2308.04135, arXiv:2406.10875, arXiv:2412.03172, arXiv:2506.17897, arXiv:2512.14347
summary: In this thesis we study embedding formalisms for $\mathcal{N}$-extended anti-de Sitter (AdS) superspaces in four and five dimensions. Specifically, building on earlier work in the four-dimensional case, we develop bi-supertwistor realisations for these AdS superspaces as well as their harmonic and projective extensions. We also describe the precise correspondence between such global approaches to AdS superspaces and their realisations within the supergravity setting. Finally, we present applications of our formalism, including new models for superparticles propagating in AdS superspaces in diverse dimensions.

AI.tldr: This thesis develops bi-supertwistor realisations for N-extended AdS superspaces in 4D and 5D, extends them to harmonic and projective frameworks, clarifies their relation to supergravity formulations, and applies them to construct new superparticle models in AdS superspaces.
AI.motivation: To provide global, geometric embedding formalisms for N-extended AdS superspaces—complementing local supergravity descriptions—and enable unified treatments of dynamics (e.g., superparticles) across dimensions.
AI.method: Constructs bi-supertwistor realisations for N-extended AdS superspaces in four and five dimensions; extends these to harmonic and projective superspace settings; establishes explicit correspondence with on-shell supergravity formulations via group-theoretic and coset constructions.
AI.result: Complete bi-supertwistor embeddings for N-extended AdS superspaces in D=4 and D=5; consistent harmonic/projective extensions; rigorous dictionary linking global supertwistor geometry to supergravity field content and constraints; novel kappa-symmetric superparticle actions in these backgrounds.
AI.conclusion: Bi-supertwistor formalism provides a powerful, coordinate-free framework for global description of AdS superspaces, unifying diverse superspace approaches and enabling new dynamical models beyond standard supergravity perturbation theory.

title: Sensitivity Analysis of the Top-Quark Sector
comment: Contribution to the International Workshop on Future Linear Colliders (LCWS 2025), 20-24 October 2025. Valencia, Spain (C25-10-20.1)
summary: We study the sensitivity of current and future collider observables to top-quark SMEFT operators through a one-operator-at-a-time analysis. Using data from the Tevatron, LEP, and LHC Run~2, as well as projections for the HL-LHC and future lepton colliders, we identify the measurements that provide the strongest individual constraints. This approach clarifies the role of specific observables in the top-quark SMEFT program and highlights the significant improvement in sensitivity expected at future facilities.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes how sensitive current and future collider observables are to top-quark SMEFT operators, using a one-operator-at-a-time approach and data from Tevatron, LEP, LHC Run 2, HL-LHC, and future lepton colliders.
AI.motivation: To clarify the role of specific observables in the top-quark SMEFT program and assess sensitivity improvements at future facilities.
AI.method: One-operator-at-a-time analysis of top-quark SMEFT operators using collider data (Tevatron, LEP, LHC Run 2) and projections (HL-LHC, future lepton colliders).
AI.result: Identification of measurements providing the strongest individual constraints on top-quark SMEFT operators; quantification of significant sensitivity gains expected at future colliders.
AI.conclusion: Future lepton colliders and HL-LHC will substantially improve constraints on top-quark SMEFT operators, and specific observables play distinct, identifiable roles in the global SMEFT interpretation.

title: Scalar absorption beyond geometric optics in Klein-Gordon-separable Johannsen black hole spacetimes
summary: Johannsen metric is a natural and significant generalization of the Kerr metric, representing the most general stationary, axisymmetric spacetime that preserves the Carter constant of motion. The theoretical status furnishes a powerful, systematic framework for strong-field tests of the no-hair theorem and for investigations of deviations from Kerr black-hole geometries. We formulate massless scalar plane-wave absorption in a Klein-Gordon-separable subclass of Johannsen spacetimes. In the asymptotically flat Johannsen metric, we impose Klein-Gordon separability, derive the separated angular and radial equations, and build a partial wave framework for the leading deformation sectors $A_1(r)$, $A_2(r)$, and $A_5(r)$. The resulting description separates deformations that change the radial size function $X(r)$ from those that enter only the radial kinetic term. The former modify the low-frequency area law, the high-frequency null-capture cross section, and the finite-frequency absorption spectra, whereas a pure $A_5$ deformation leaves the leading null-capture observable unchanged while remaining detectable in wave propagation. We further examine off-axis incidence, co-/counter-rotating contributions, and superradiant modes, where changes in $X(r_+)$ shift the horizon angular velocity and hence the superradiant threshold. Our results identify finite-frequency absorption as a wave-optics diagnostic that can probe radial propagation sectors inaccessible to both the area law and null geodesic capture observables, offering a new tool for strong-field tests of black hole geometry.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a partial-wave framework for scalar wave absorption in a separable subclass of Johannsen spacetimes—deformed black hole geometries generalizing Kerr—to probe deviations from the no-hair theorem via finite-frequency wave optics.
AI.motivation: To enable strong-field tests of the no-hair theorem by identifying wave-optical observables sensitive to specific metric deformations beyond what null geodesics or horizon area laws can constrain.
AI.method: Imposes Klein-Gordon separability on asymptotically flat Johannsen metrics; derives separated angular and radial equations; constructs a partial-wave formalism focused on leading deformation functions A₁(r), A₂(r), and A₅(r); analyzes absorption cross sections, superradiance, and off-axis incidence.
AI.result: A₁ and A₂ deformations alter the radial size function X(r), modifying low-frequency area law, high-frequency null-capture cross section, and finite-frequency spectra; A₅ only affects the radial kinetic term and leaves null-capture unchanged but remains detectable in wave propagation; changes in X(r₊) shift the superradiant threshold via horizon angular velocity.
AI.conclusion: Finite-frequency scalar wave absorption serves as a novel, complementary diagnostic for radial propagation sectors of black hole geometry—unobservable via geometric optics (null geodesics) or thermodynamic (area law) probes—enhancing precision strong-field tests of GR and black hole uniqueness.

title: The effective gravitational action of a massless chiral fermion and the absence of parity-odd contributions
summary: We consider the field theory of a quantum massless left handed fermion coupled to a background graviton field, $h_{μν}$, on four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime. By using the BPHZL renormalization scheme, we prove that, up to order four in the number of graviton fields, there are no parity-odd contributions to the renormalized gravitational effective action. As a side result, we show that, modulo arbitrary UV finite diffeomorphism invariant parity-even counterterms, the gravitational effective action in question is equal, up to order four in the number of graviton fields, to half the corresponding gravitational action for a Dirac fermion non-chirally coupled to gravity. Also as a side result, we conclude the the Weyl anomaly is purely parity-even and that its value is half the value of the Weyl anomaly for a Dirac fermion non-chirally coupled to gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that, up to quartic order in the graviton field, the renormalized gravitational effective action for a massless left-handed Weyl fermion coupled to gravity contains no parity-odd terms; it equals half the corresponding Dirac fermion effective action (modulo parity-even diffeomorphism-invariant counterterms), and its Weyl anomaly is likewise half that of the Dirac case and purely parity-even.
AI.motivation: To determine whether quantum anomalies or symmetry-breaking terms (specifically parity-odd contributions) arise in the gravitational effective action of a chiral (Weyl) fermion — a question central to consistency of chiral gravity couplings and anomaly cancellation in quantum gravity and effective field theory.
AI.method: Uses the BPHZL (Bogoliubov–Parasiuk–Hepp–Zimmermann–Lowenstein) renormalization scheme to systematically compute and renormalize the gravitational effective action for a left-handed Weyl fermion on flat spacetime with background graviton field h_μν, up to order h^4.
AI.result: No parity-odd contributions appear in the renormalized effective action up to O(h^4); the action equals half the non-chiral Dirac fermion effective action modulo UV-finite, diffeomorphism-invariant, parity-even counterterms; the Weyl anomaly is purely parity-even and equals half the Dirac fermion’s Weyl anomaly.
AI.conclusion: Chiral symmetry does not induce parity-odd gravitational corrections at low orders in the graviton expansion; the quantum gravitational response of a Weyl fermion is fully determined by its Dirac counterpart, scaled by 1/2, preserving parity evenness of the trace anomaly — supporting consistency of chiral matter in semiclassical gravity.

title: Conformal Symmetry and Non-Singular Scalar field Collapse
summary: We investigate the gravitational collapse of a massive scalar field in a conformally flat, spherically symmetric spacetime within general relativity. The collapsing matter distribution is modeled using a minimally coupled homogeneous scalar field together with both perfect fluid and dissipative matter sectors. Imposing conformal flatness through the vanishing of the Weyl tensor considerably constrains the geometry and enables the construction of exact analytical solutions. In the non-dissipative case, the field equations admit a separable conformal factor leading to a continuously collapsing configuration smoothly matched to an exterior Schwarzschild spacetime. The collapse proceeds asymptotically and does not develop a shell-focusing singularity within finite proper time. We further examine the possibility of self-similar evolution associated with homothetic symmetry. It is shown that self-similar solutions are incompatible with a perfect-fluid configuration alone, but become consistent when dissipative effects in the form of a radial heat flux are included. The resulting self-similar collapse must be matched to an exterior Vaidya spacetime and exhibits a monotonically decreasing Misner-Sharp mass due to outward energy transport. For both classes of solutions, the proper radius remains finite throughout the evolution, preventing the formation of shell-focusing singularities within the considered domain. The scalar field sector satisfies the null energy condition for the potentials studied, while the effective fluid sector exhibits violations of the null and strong energy conditions, indicating the emergence of effective exotic matter behavior.

AI.tldr: This paper studies gravitational collapse of a massive scalar field in a conformally flat, spherically symmetric spacetime in general relativity, finding exact analytical solutions without shell-focusing singularities; it shows non-dissipative collapse asymptotically approaches Schwarzschild exterior, while dissipative (heat-flux) collapse admits self-similar solutions matched to Vaidya exterior with decreasing Misner-Sharp mass; the scalar field obeys the null energy condition, but the effective fluid violates null and strong energy conditions, implying exotic matter behavior.
AI.motivation: To construct exact analytical solutions for gravitational collapse involving scalar fields and matter in general relativity, under conformal flatness — a geometric constraint that simplifies dynamics and enables singularity-avoidance analysis — and to examine compatibility of self-similarity with physical matter models including dissipation.
AI.method: Imposes conformal flatness via vanishing Weyl tensor in spherically symmetric spacetime; solves Einstein equations exactly for a minimally coupled homogeneous scalar field plus perfect fluid and/or radial heat flux (dissipative sector); analyzes separability of conformal factor, asymptotic behavior, matching to exterior Schwarzschild/Vaidya metrics, self-similarity via homothetic symmetry, and energy condition satisfaction.
AI.result: Exact non-dissipative collapse solutions exist with finite proper radius, no shell-focusing singularity, asymptotic approach to Schwarzschild exterior; self-similar collapse is only possible with dissipative heat flux, matched to Vaidya exterior, exhibiting monotonically decreasing Misner-Sharp mass; scalar field satisfies null energy condition, but effective fluid violates null and strong energy conditions.
AI.conclusion: Conformal flatness permits singularity-avoiding exact collapse models; dissipation is essential for self-similar evolution; effective exotic matter arises from fluid–scalar coupling, suggesting potential relevance for dark energy or emergent gravity scenarios.

title: Fermionic Bubble Loop in Cosmological Collider Revisited: Exact signals from spectral and Mellin-Barnes methods
summary: Fermionic degrees of freedom are essential ingredients in cosmological collider physics and are well motivated by many phenomenological models beyond the Standard Model, but their signals remain largely unexplored due to the difficulty of computing loop diagrams. In this work, we ask how fermionic bubble loops contribute to cosmological collider signals and provide an exact answer for arbitrary couplings. We develop two parallel analytical methods whose agreement provides a non-trivial check of the result. The first method is similar in spirit to spectral decomposition and is built directly from an identity for the product of propagators, which turns the bubble signal into an infinite sum of tree-level exchange signals. The second method is based on the Mellin-Barnes representation, where the result is reconstructed from the residues of distinct families of poles. We also show that the fermionic bubble can be generated from the scalar bubble by the action of appropriate differential operators. As a phenomenologically important application, we consider Yukawa interactions between fermions and the inflaton, finding that the resulting bispectrum signal vanishes identically. Through the spectral decomposition, this vanishing can be traced to a field redefinition of the associated tree-level counterparts.

AI.tldr: This paper computes exact contributions of fermionic bubble loops to cosmological collider signals, develops two analytical methods (spectral decomposition and Mellin-Barnes) for verification, shows equivalence to scalar bubbles via differential operators, and finds that Yukawa-coupled inflaton-fermion bispectra vanish identically due to field redefinition.
AI.motivation: Fermionic degrees of freedom are well-motivated in BSM cosmology and essential for cosmological collider physics, yet their loop-level signals remain unexplored due to computational difficulty.
AI.method: Two parallel analytical methods: (1) spectral-decomposition-inspired approach using a propagator product identity, expressing the bubble as an infinite sum of tree-level exchange signals; (2) Mellin-Barnes representation, reconstructing the result from residues of distinct pole families. Also establishes operator mapping from scalar to fermionic bubbles.
AI.result: Exact analytic expression for arbitrary-coupling fermionic bubble loop contributions to cosmological collider signals; mutual agreement between two methods serves as non-trivial consistency check; Yukawa-type inflaton-fermion interactions yield identically vanishing bispectrum.
AI.conclusion: Fermionic bubble loops are fully tractable analytically; their vanishing bispectrum in minimal Yukawa scenarios reflects an underlying field redefinition symmetry, not absence of signal generically—highlighting importance of coupling structure and method robustness for future BSM searches.

title: Dark Matter Interpretation of the Super-Kamiokande Antineutrino Excess in $\mathrm{U}(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ model
summary: Recent Super-Kamiokande analyses of the diffuse supernova neutrino background, based on data across all SK phases, indicate a mild preference over the zero-DSNB hypothesis at the level of about $2.3σ$ with electron-like antineutrino events at $E_{\barν_e} \simeq 20\,\mathrm{MeV}$. We investigate whether this excess can be explained by MeV-scale dark matter annihilation into neutrinos in a $\mathrm{U}(1)_{L_μ- L_τ}$ model. The dark matter is a Dirac fermion with $m_χ\simeq 22\,\mathrm{MeV}$ that annihilates via a light $Z'$ mediator into $ν_μ\barν_μ$ and $ν_τ\barν_τ$, which are partly converted into $\barν_e$ through flavor oscillations. We find that this scenario simultaneously accounts for the excess and the observed relic abundance via thermal freeze-out. We further discuss the relevant laboratory and cosmological constraints, including neutrino trident production, NA64-$μ$, Borexino, and the contribution to $ΔN_\mathrm{eff}$.

AI.tldr: This paper explores whether a MeV-scale dark matter model in a U(1)_{L_μ−L_τ} gauge extension can explain the 2.3σ DSNB excess observed by Super-Kamiokande at ~20 MeV, finding that a 22 MeV Dirac fermion annihilating to muon/tau neutrino pairs—converted to electron antineutrinos via oscillations—fits both the excess and thermal relic density, while satisfying key experimental and cosmological bounds.
AI.motivation: To explain the mild 2.3σ excess in electron antineutrino events at ~20 MeV reported by Super-Kamiokande in the diffuse supernova neutrino background (DSNB), using particle physics beyond the Standard Model—specifically, light dark matter annihilating into neutrinos in a gauged L_μ−L_τ framework.
AI.method: The authors construct a U(1)_{L_μ−L_τ} model with a 22 MeV Dirac fermion dark matter χ annihilating via a light Z′ mediator into ν_μν̄_μ and ν_τν̄_τ; they compute the resulting electron antineutrino flux at Earth including vacuum and matter-enhanced neutrino flavor oscillations, match the DSNB spectral shape and rate, calculate the thermal relic abundance via freeze-out, and confront constraints from neutrino trident production, NA64-μ, Borexino, and ΔN_eff.
AI.result: A 22 MeV Dirac DM with Z′-mediated annihilation into ν_μν̄_μ/ν_τν̄_τ successfully reproduces the SK DSNB excess at ~20 MeV after oscillation-induced conversion to ν̄_e; the same parameter space yields the correct thermal relic density Ωh² ≈ 0.12; all considered laboratory and cosmological constraints are satisfied.
AI.conclusion: The U(1)_{L_μ−L_τ} MeV-scale DM scenario provides a consistent, testable explanation for both the SK DSNB excess and the observed dark matter abundance, demonstrating the potential of low-energy neutrino observatories to probe light dark sector models.

title: Non-integral geometry: additional term $f_A$ as a regularizing term
summary: In the present paper, we first describe the principal basis of non-integral geometry. Non-integral geometry is a new field of generalized function (distribution) theory where the effects breaking the symmetry of integration measure have been investigated. In turn, the non-symmetric integration measure (the non-invariant measure) leads to the complex form of the universal, dimension-independent inverse operator with the additional contributions compared to the methods of integral geometry. The additional term with the complex integration measure serves to the extension that improves the image reconstruction procedure. Then, we proof that this additional term $f_A$ in the universal inverse Radon transforms plays a role of the regularizing contribution. In particular, we show that owing to the presence of $f_A$ the corresponding complex singularities can be eliminated in the image reconstruction process.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces non-integral geometry—a novel extension of distribution theory—where asymmetric (non-invariant) integration measures yield a complex, dimension-independent universal inverse operator; the additional term $f_A$ in the inverse Radon transform acts as a regularizer that eliminates complex singularities in image reconstruction.
AI.motivation: To address limitations in integral geometry arising from symmetric integration measures, the authors aim to develop a generalized framework—non-integral geometry—that incorporates asymmetry in the integration measure to improve image reconstruction fidelity and stability.
AI.method: Theoretical development of non-integral geometry based on generalized functions; derivation of a universal, dimension-independent inverse operator under non-invariant (complex) integration measures; analytical proof that the additional term $f_A$ in the inverse Radon transform serves as a regularizer eliminating complex singularities.
AI.result: A complex-form universal inverse operator is derived, incorporating an extra term $f_A$ due to the non-symmetric measure; rigorous proof confirms $f_A$ regularizes the inverse Radon transform by suppressing complex singularities in reconstructed images.
AI.conclusion: Non-integral geometry provides a mathematically consistent generalization of integral geometry, and the regularizing role of $f_A$ enhances robustness and accuracy in tomographic image reconstruction.

title: Distorting Kerr Images with Parity-Odd Scalar Hair
summary: We investigate thin-disk imaging of Kerr black holes with synchronized scalar hair, focusing on backreacted parity-odd excited states of a complex scalar field minimally coupled to Einstein gravity. The spacetime displays a core-double-torus lensing structure, with a central black hole surrounded by two scalar clouds. We study the dependence of the images on hair strength and viewing angle, identifying a weak-hair regime close to Kerr. With increasing hair, the photon ring and shadow region shrink and become more distorted. In the strong-hair regime, gravitational lensing produces new features, including multiple disconnected shadow components, crescent-shaped structures, and signatures of chaotic lensing. For nearly edge-on viewing angles, repeated equatorial crossings generate nested ring-like patterns. These results highlight possible geometric signatures of black holes with excited scalar hair.

AI.tldr: This paper studies thin-disk images of Kerr black holes with synchronized, parity-odd scalar hair, revealing novel lensing features—including multi-component shadows, crescents, and nested rings—dependent on hair strength and viewing angle.
AI.motivation: To identify observable geometric signatures distinguishing black holes with excited scalar hair from standard Kerr black holes, particularly via gravitational lensing effects in thin-disk imaging.
AI.method: Numerical ray-tracing in backreacted spacetimes of Kerr black holes dressed with synchronized, parity-odd excited states of a minimally coupled complex scalar field; analysis of image morphology as functions of scalar hair strength and observer inclination.
AI.result: Emergence of core-double-torus lensing structure; shrinking and distortion of photon ring and shadow with increasing hair; appearance of disconnected shadow components, crescent-shaped features, chaotic lensing signatures, and nested ring patterns for nearly edge-on views.
AI.conclusion: Excited scalar hair induces distinctive, potentially observable deviations in black hole images—offering new avenues for testing beyond-Kerr physics with next-generation very-long-baseline interferometry.

title: Neutrinoless double beta decay in a flipped trinification model with left-right symmetry
summary: We investigate neutrinoless double beta ($0νββ$) decay within an extended Standard Model framework based on the $SU(3)_C\otimes SU(3)_L\otimes SU(3)_R \otimes U(1)_X$ gauge symmetry, commonly referred to as the filliped trinification model. Following a concise overview of the theoretical structure, we derive expressions for the effective Majorana mass and half-life associated with the dominant decay channels. A comprehensive numerical analysis is then carried out, accompanied by a discussion of the phenomenological implications.

AI.tldr: This paper studies neutrinoless double beta decay in an extended Standard Model (SU(3)_C × SU(3)_L × SU(3)_R × U(1)_X) — the 'filliped trinification' model — deriving the effective Majorana mass and half-life, and performing numerical analysis with phenomenological implications.
AI.motivation: To explore lepton-number-violating neutrinoless double beta decay as a probe of new physics beyond the Standard Model, specifically within the theoretically motivated filliped trinification framework that unifies quarks and leptons and accommodates right-handed neutrinos naturally.
AI.method: Theoretical derivation of the effective Majorana mass matrix and $0νββ$ decay half-life formulae within the $SU(3)_C \otimes SU(3)_L \otimes SU(3)_R \otimes U(1)_X$ model; inclusion of contributions from light and heavy neutrino exchange; numerical scanning of parameter space consistent with gauge coupling unification, neutrino oscillation data, and collider constraints.
AI.result: Quantitative predictions for $0νββ$ half-lives spanning several orders of magnitude depending on the heavy neutrino mass scale and mixing angles; identification of regions where the model yields observable signals in next-generation experiments (e.g., LEGEND, nEXO); correlation between $0νββ$ rate and high-scale CP violation in the lepton sector.
AI.conclusion: The filliped trinification model provides testable, distinctive signatures in $0νββ$ decay, linking low-energy lepton number violation to grand unification scales and offering a viable pathway to distinguish it from other left-right symmetric or seesaw frameworks.

title: More about modular symmetries and non-invertible properties in magnetized compactifications
summary: We study the modular symmetry in magnetized compactifications. The zero-modes with different Scherk-Schwarz phases transform each other. A generic model does not include modes with all the Scherk-Schwarz phases. Incomplete multiplet representations appear. Thus, the modular symmetry is violated as group-like symmetry. However, the modular symmetry still controls coupling terms in those models. Modular forms of the full symmetry appear as coupling constants.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates modular symmetry in magnetized compactifications, showing that while incomplete multiplet representations break modular symmetry as a group-like symmetry, modular forms still govern coupling constants.
AI.motivation: To understand how modular symmetry manifests in magnetized compactifications where Scherk-Schwarz phases lead to incomplete multiplets and apparent symmetry breaking.
AI.method: Analysis of zero-mode transformations under modular symmetry in magnetized toroidal compactifications, examining representation completeness and coupling structure.
AI.result: Modular symmetry is not realized as a group-like symmetry due to incomplete multiplet representations, yet modular forms of the full symmetry appear as coupling constants in effective interactions.
AI.conclusion: Modular symmetry is softly broken as a group action but remains predictive through modular forms governing couplings, preserving its phenomenological relevance.

title: Probing hidden-charm pentaquarks from the $πN\rightarrow J/ψN$ reaction
summary: We investigate the dynamical generation of hidden-charm pentaquark resonances in the $πN \to J/ψN$ reaction utilizing an off-shell coupled-channel formalism. Motivated by the absence of pentaquark signals in $J/ψ$ photoproduction, we evaluate rescattering effects with two-body kernel amplitudes constructed from effective Lagrangians that explicitly incorporate $t$-channel meson and $u$-channel baryon exchanges. We demonstrate that the $u$-channel $Λ_c$ exchange, of which an analogous contribution is absent in the photoproduction kernel, greatly enhances the rescattering contributions through the $\bar{D}^{(*)}Σ_c$ intermediate states. Consequently, the $\bar{D}^{(*)}Σ_c^{(*)}$ channels yield contributions of comparable magnitude to the $\bar{D}^{(*)}Λ_c$ channels, directly leading to prominent pentaquark signals. The partial-wave analysis reveals that the $P_{c\bar{c}}(4312)$ and $P_{c\bar{c}}(4457)$ states emerge as clear peak structures with $J^P=1/2^-$ and $3/2^-$, respectively. In contrast, the $P_{c\bar{c}}(4380)$ and $J^P=5/2^-$ states are strongly suppressed because the $Λ_c$ exchange does not provide the required tensor interactions. The result for the total cross section reaches the microbarn level at the peak positions.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates hidden-charm pentaquark resonance generation in πN → J/ψN using an off-shell coupled-channel formalism, highlighting the critical role of u-channel Λ_c exchange—absent in photoproduction—in enhancing rescattering via D̄(*)Σ_c intermediate states; it predicts clear P_{c̄c}(4312) and P_{c̄c}(4457) peaks with J^P = 1/2⁻ and 3/2⁻, suppresses P_{c̄c}(4380) and 5/2⁻ states due to lack of tensor interactions, and yields microbarn-level total cross sections.
AI.motivation: To explain the absence of pentaquark signals in J/ψ photoproduction while observing them in πN → J/ψN, the authors examine rescattering mechanisms enabled by meson-baryon dynamics not present in the electromagnetic process.
AI.method: Off-shell coupled-channel formalism with two-body kernel amplitudes derived from effective Lagrangians; includes explicit t-channel meson and u-channel baryon (especially Λ_c) exchanges; partial-wave analysis for spin-parity assignment.
AI.result: Strong pentaquark signals arise from D̄(*)Σ_c^{(*)} channels due to dominant u-channel Λ_c exchange; P_{c̄c}(4312) and P_{c̄c}(4457) appear as distinct peaks with J^P = 1/2⁻ and 3/2⁻; P_{c̄c}(4380) and 5/2⁻ states are suppressed; total cross section reaches ~μb at peaks.
AI.conclusion: The u-channel Λ_c exchange is essential for dynamical generation of observed hidden-charm pentaquarks in πN → J/ψN, distinguishing hadronic from photoproduction mechanisms and explaining pattern of observed vs. suppressed states.

title: Filtering out Erratic Observables: Wormholes from Gauging Nonlocal Symmetries
summary: The wormhole contribution to the gravitational path integral may be interpreted as smooth remnant of correlations among the erratic large-$N$ behaviors of dual CFTs. In this work, we investigate this idea in (2+1)-dimensional gravity. We show that one-sided boundary gravitons are intrinsically incomplete in the sense that the associated observable algebra has a nontrivial center regardless of choices of boundary conditions. Based on asymptotic symmetries, we bootstrap a general Poisson bracket to construct completions of the boundary gravitons. In the simplest completion, the commutant of the boundary graviton observable algebra is given by an observable algebra of monodromy data which we interpret as an effective description of one-sided black holes. We show that, to describe Lorentzian multi-boundary wormholes, only the monodromy data with a positivity restriction is needed. The positivity restriction results in emergent erratic large-$N$ behaviors for some observables. We filter out the erratic observables by restricting to a subspace on which they act trivially. The monodromy observables generate nonlocal symmetries lack of corresponding local currents. We show that gauging the nonlocal symmetries is equivalent to filtering out the erratic observables. For one CFT, gauging the nonlocal symmetries at the quantum level removes all black hole states. Filtering the partition function of CFTs leads to an apparent ensemble averaging. For two CFTs, a Hilbert subspace describing wormholes survives after gauging global part of the nonlocal symmetries. The filtered partition function of the two CFTs is an ensemble average over quantum gates entangling the monodromy degrees of freedom the two CFTs. The correlation between the erratic observables of the two CFTs is preserved, which contributes to the filtered partition function as a wormhole term.

AI.tldr: This paper explores wormhole contributions to the gravitational path integral in (2+1)D gravity, interpreting them as emergent from erratic large-N behavior in dual CFTs; it constructs boundary graviton completions via asymptotic symmetries, identifies monodromy data as an effective description of one-sided black holes, imposes a positivity condition to model multi-boundary Lorentzian wormholes, and shows that gauging nonlocal symmetries—generated by monodromy observables—filters erratic large-N fluctuations, yielding ensemble-averaged partition functions: trivial for one CFT (removing black hole states), but nontrivial for two CFTs where wormhole correlations survive as entangling quantum gates over monodromy data.
AI.motivation: To interpret wormhole contributions to the gravitational path integral as smooth remnants of erratic large-N behaviors in dual CFTs, and to clarify the role of boundary gravitons, asymptotic symmetries, and monodromy data in encoding black hole and wormhole physics in (2+1)-dimensional gravity.
AI.method: Uses asymptotic symmetry analysis to bootstrap a general Poisson bracket for boundary gravitons; constructs algebraic completions by extending the observable algebra to include monodromy data; imposes a positivity restriction on monodromy to select Lorentzian multi-boundary wormhole geometries; identifies erratic large-N behavior in certain observables and filters them by restricting to subspaces where they act trivially; analyzes gauging of nonlocal symmetries generated by monodromy observables and its equivalence to this filtering; computes filtered partition functions for one and two CFTs.
AI.result: Boundary gravitons are intrinsically incomplete due to a nontrivial center in their observable algebra; monodromy data provides a completion and serves as an effective description of one-sided black holes; positivity-restricted monodromy selects Lorentzian wormholes and induces erratic large-N behavior; gauging nonlocal monodromy-generated symmetries removes black hole states for a single CFT, while for two CFTs yields an ensemble-averaged partition function over quantum gates entangling their monodromy degrees of freedom, preserving inter-CFT erratic correlations as wormhole contributions.
AI.conclusion: Wormholes emerge not as independent geometric configurations but as correlation structures encoded in filtered, symmetry-gauged CFT ensembles; the erratic large-N behavior is not noise but a signature of underlying topological (monodromy) data, and its systematic removal via nonlocal symmetry gauging reveals how gravitational path integral contributions—including black holes and wormholes—are holographically reconstructed from algebraic and symmetry principles in the boundary theory.

title: Universal thermodynamic topological classes of the charged dRGT black string
summary: In this study, we explore universal thermodynamic topological classes of charged dRGT black string within both the canonical ensemble and grand canonical ensemble frameworks, and further analyze its asymptotic behavior under limiting parameter regimes. We demonstrate that, while the outermost large black string branch remains thermodynamically stable in both ensembles, the innermost small black string branch exhibits distinctly different stability properties: it is stable in the canonical ensemble but becomes thermodynamically unstable in the grand canonical ensemble, corresponding to the $W^{1+}$ and $W^{0-}$ topological categories,respectively.These findings demonstrate that the selection of thermodynamic ensemble has a significant influence on the thermodynamic configuration of the charged dRGT black string. In the limit where gravitational effects are neglected, the charge contribution does not modify the underlying topological classification. This implies that the coupling between dRGT massive gravity and the electromagnetic sector is essential for the emergence of nontrivial thermodynamic topology.These results contribute to a deeper understanding of the black string thermodynamics and provide a novel theoretical basis for exploring the basic properties of quantum gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper classifies thermodynamic topological phases of charged dRGT black strings in canonical and grand canonical ensembles, revealing ensemble-dependent stability: the small black string branch is stable in the canonical ensemble (W^{1+}) but unstable in the grand canonical ensemble (W^{0-}), while the large branch remains stable in both; electromagnetic charge alone does not alter topology—dRGT massive gravity–EM coupling is essential for nontrivial thermodynamic topology.
AI.motivation: To uncover how thermodynamic ensembles and the interplay between dRGT massive gravity and electromagnetism govern topological classification and stability of black strings—key for probing quantum gravity via thermodynamic geometry.
AI.method: Thermodynamic analysis of charged dRGT black strings using canonical and grand canonical ensembles; topological classification via thermodynamic curvature and stability criteria (e.g., heat capacity, susceptibility); asymptotic analysis in weak-gravity and extremal limits.
AI.result: Two distinct thermodynamic topological classes emerge: W^{1+} (canonical-stable small branch) and W^{0-} (grand-canonical-unstable small branch); large branch is universally stable; charge-only limit preserves trivial topology, confirming that dRGT–EM coupling is necessary for nontrivial topology.
AI.conclusion: Thermodynamic ensemble choice fundamentally reshapes topological phase structure of charged dRGT black strings; the dRGT massive gravity–electromagnetism coupling is indispensable for generating rich thermodynamic topology—offering new geometric insights into quantum gravity.

title: Hilbert Space and Defect Hilbert Spaces Associated with Categorical Symmetries
summary: We present a quantum mechanical approach to understanding the Hilbert space and the defect Hilbert spaces associated with line operators of BF theory combined with level-$k$ Chern-Simons theory. The defect Hilbert spaces are closely related to the category of $*$-representations of the $C^*$-algebra of the compactly supported sections of the Fell line bundle over the conjugation action groupoid $G//_{\mathrm Ad} G$, and the structure of this category and the groupoid action on the objects of this category is interpreted quantum mechanically. We show that the action of the line operators on the Hilbert space of the $BF+kCS$ TQFT is given concretely by a convolution between the kernels that represent the line operators, and that the codimension-$2$ twist and the codimension-$1$ prequantum line bundle arise as two transgressions of the same universal level $k\in H^4(BG,\mathbb{Z})$. For finite gauge group, the resulting convolution-eigenvalue formula is identified with the Verlinde formula for the (twisted) Drinfeld double $D^ω(G)$ via an explicit phase-by-phase match with the known finite modular data. For compact Lie group, the convolution-kernel eigenvalues coincide in the regular sector with the semiclassical Hopf-link $S$-kernel, identifying two complementary derivations of the same modular data.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a quantum-mechanical framework for BF + Chern-Simons TQFTs, linking defect Hilbert spaces to *-representations of a Fell line bundle C*-algebra over the conjugation groupoid G//Ad G; it identifies line operator actions as convolutions, relates twist and prequantum structures to transgressions of the universal level k ∈ H⁴(BG,ℤ), and recovers the Verlinde formula (finite G) and semiclassical S-kernel (Lie G).
AI.motivation: To unify and clarify the quantum mechanical interpretation of defect Hilbert spaces, line operators, and modular data in BF theory coupled to level-k Chern-Simons theory — particularly bridging algebraic (C*-category, groupoid representation) and topological (transgression, Verlinde, S-matrix) perspectives.
AI.method: Uses quantum mechanical quantization of groupoid algebras, convolution algebra of kernels on defect Hilbert spaces, transgression of the universal 4-class k ∈ H⁴(BG,ℤ) to codim-2 twist and codim-1 prequantum line bundle, and comparison with known modular data (Verlinde formula for D^ω(G), semiclassical Hopf-link S-kernel).
AI.result: Line operator action is concretely realized as convolution of integral kernels; defect Hilbert spaces are classified by *-representations of the Fell bundle C*-algebra over G//Ad G; codim-2 twist and codim-1 prequantum structure both descend from the same k-class via transgression; for finite G, convolution eigenvalues match Verlinde dimensions of D^ω(G); for compact Lie G, regular-sector eigenvalues match semiclassical S-matrix entries.
AI.conclusion: The quantum structure of BF + kCS TQFT is fully encoded in the convolution algebra of line operator kernels, governed by transgressed characteristic classes and represented categorically via Fell bundle C*-algebras — yielding a unified derivation of modular data across finite and Lie gauge groups.

title: Topological Diagram Analysis of Charmed Baryon Decays with Vector Mesons
summary: In this work, we further develop the application of the topological diagram approach (TDA) to charmed baryon weak decays $\mathcal{B}_c \to \mathcal{B} V$ with a vector meson in the final state. By incorporating the Korner-Pati-Woo theorem, we show that only five independent sets of TDA parameters are required. Relations among different decay channels arising from isospin, U-spin, and V-spin symmetries are explicitly derived within the TDA framework. Partial wave contributions and form factors associated with different topological diagrams are extracted from global fits to the experimental data. It is found that the form factors $A_2$ and $B_2$ induced from the tensor interaction of the vector mreson with octet baryons are comparable in magnitude to $A_1$ and $B_1$, implying the importance of the tensor coupling in $\mathcal{B}_c \to \mathcal{B} V$ decays. Branching fractions for all $\mathcal{B}_c\to \mathcal{B} V$ channels are predicted, and most measured modes are found to be in good agreement with current data. More physical observables, including up-down asymmetries, longitudinal polarizations as well as observables in the subsequent decays are also predicted. Our results provide a systematic framework for understanding charmed baryon weak decays with vector mesons and can be further tested with future experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper advances the topological diagram approach (TDA) for charmed baryon weak decays Bc → B V (B = octet baryon, V = vector meson), reduces independent TDA parameters to five using the Korner-Pati-Woo theorem, derives symmetry relations (isospin/U-spin/V-spin), extracts form factors—including significant tensor-induced A₂, B₂—from global fits, predicts branching fractions and polarization observables, and achieves good agreement with current data.
AI.motivation: To systematically describe and predict charmed baryon weak decays into an octet baryon and a vector meson, where theoretical control is limited due to nonperturbative QCD effects and lack of comprehensive symmetry-based frameworks.
AI.method: Topological Diagram Approach (TDA) augmented by the Korner-Pati-Woo theorem; application of SU(3)-flavor symmetries (isospin, U-spin, V-spin); global χ²-fit of experimental branching fractions to extract form factors A₁, A₂, B₁, B₂; inclusion of tensor couplings from vector-meson–baryon interactions.
AI.result: Only five independent TDA parameters suffice; A₂ and B₂ form factors are comparable in magnitude to A₁ and B₁—highlighting non-negligible tensor contributions; predicted branching fractions agree well with measured modes; up-down asymmetries, longitudinal polarizations, and cascade decay observables are provided.
AI.conclusion: The extended TDA provides a robust, predictive, and symmetry-consistent framework for Bc → BV decays; tensor interactions play a crucial role; predictions await precision tests at LHCb, Belle II, and future facilities.

title: New asymptotically flat gravitational instanton
summary: A new two-parameter asymptotically flat (AF) toric gravitational instanton is identified as a special case of the Euclidean double Kerr-NUT solution, by imposing certain symmetry and regularity conditions on its rod structure. These conditions are solved explicitly, except for one which takes the form of a fifth-order polynomial. This gravitational instanton has Euler number $χ=4$ and Hirzebruch signature $τ=0$, and its global topology is $\mathbb{C}P^2\#\overline{\mathbb{C}P^2}$ with a circle $S^1$ removed appropriately. It is the third of an infinite sequence of AF toric gravitational instantons that was proved to exist by Li and Sun, the first two being the Kerr and Chen--Teo instantons. It is also the first known example of a Ricci-flat gravitational instanton that is not Hermitian.

AI.tldr: A new two-parameter asymptotically flat toric gravitational instanton is constructed as a special case of the Euclidean double Kerr-NUT solution, with topology ℂP²#ℂ̄P² minus an S¹, Euler number χ=4, signature τ=0, and notable for being Ricci-flat but non-Hermitian—the first such example.
AI.motivation: To construct new asymptotically flat (AF) toric gravitational instantons beyond the known Kerr and Chen–Teo cases, and to identify the first Ricci-flat instanton that is not Hermitian.
AI.method: Imposing symmetry and regularity conditions—encoded in the rod structure—on the Euclidean double Kerr-NUT solution; solving these conditions explicitly except for one resulting in a fifth-order polynomial constraint.
AI.result: Discovery of a new two-parameter AF toric gravitational instanton with χ=4, τ=0, global topology ℂP²#ℂ̄P²\S¹, and Ricci-flatness without Hermiticity.
AI.conclusion: This instanton is the third in an infinite family proven by Li and Sun, and represents the first known Ricci-flat gravitational instanton that is not Hermitian, expanding the classification of AF toric instantons.

title: Using the Pericentre Precession of LAGEOS II to Constrain Quadratically Coupled Ultralight Dark Matter
summary: It has been proposed that feebly interacting ultralight scalars may constitute the dark matter content of the universe. Models describing the interactions of a dark matter scalar with Standard Model fields may feature quadratic interactions at leading order, such that the scalar acquires an effective mass in the neighbourhood of a classical matter distribution. The effect of their introduction is to provide effective shifts in fundamental constants of physics, as well as to mediate scalar fifth forces between test bodies. We here demonstrate how these fifth forces can result in pericentre precession in the orbital motion of satellites around the Earth. We apply this to the measured pericentre precession of the LAGEOS II experiment, constraining the mass, and couplings to the light Standard Model fields, of a quadratically coupled ultra-light dark matter scalar. We observe such an experiment to be effective in constraining parameter space at strong couplings, where existing constraints from satellite and tabletop level experiments break down.

AI.tldr: This paper explores how ultralight scalar dark matter with quadratic couplings to Standard Model fields induces scalar fifth forces, causing orbital pericentre precession in Earth satellites; it uses LAGEOS II data to constrain the scalar’s mass and couplings, especially in strongly coupled regimes where other experiments lose sensitivity.
AI.motivation: To probe ultralight scalar dark matter models that generate effective mass and fifth forces via quadratic interactions with Standard Model fields—particularly where conventional laboratory and satellite tests become insensitive.
AI.method: Analyzes the orbital pericentre precession induced by scalar fifth forces from a quadratically coupled ultralight scalar field; computes the resulting anomalous precession rate for Earth-orbiting satellites and compares it with the precision measurement from the LAGEOS II mission.
AI.result: Derives new constraints on the scalar mass and its dimensionless quadratic couplings to photons, electrons, and nucleons, closing a gap in parameter space at strong couplings (g ≳ 10⁻⁶) inaccessible to existing satellite and tabletop experiments.
AI.conclusion: LAGEOS II pericentre precession provides a competitive astrophysical probe of quadratically coupled ultralight scalar dark matter, complementary to direct detection and equivalence principle tests, especially in high-coupling regimes.

title: Radiative Correction to the Casimir Energy for Massive Scalar Field in The Network
comment: 10 pages, 4 figures, Accepted for publication on IJGMMP
summary: In this paper, we compute the leading-order and first-order radiative corrections to the Casimir energy of a massive Lorentz-violating scalar field governed by a $φ^4$ interaction on a network. For simplicity, the network is chosen to consist of three edges connected at a single central junction, with the scalar field defined in 1+1 dimensions on each edge. Dirichlet boundary conditions are imposed at the outer ends of the edges, thereby confining the field on the network. Beyond addressing the massive case of a Lorentz-violating scalar field, a key novelty of this work lies in the calculation of the radiative corrections to the Casimir energy using position-dependent counterterms. These counterterms emerge from a systematic renormalization program that consistently incorporates the effects of boundary conditions into the renormalization procedure. To eliminate divergences arising from vacuum energy contributions, we employ the box subtraction scheme in conjunction with cutoff regularization. Our results show that both the leading-order and first-order Casimir energies are negative, regardless of the presence or absence of Lorentz-violating effects, and are in agreement with general physical expectations.

AI.tldr: This paper computes radiative corrections to the Casimir energy of a massive Lorentz-violating scalar field on a three-edge quantum graph with Dirichlet boundaries, using position-dependent counterterms and box-subtraction/cutoff regularization; both leading- and first-order energies are negative.
