AI.motivation: To extend Casimir energy calculations to Lorentz-violating scalar fields on networks, and to develop a consistent renormalization framework incorporating boundary conditions via position-dependent counterterms.
AI.method: Computed leading-order and first-order radiative corrections to Casimir energy for a massive Lorentz-violating φ⁴ scalar field on a 1+1D star-shaped quantum graph (three edges, central junction); imposed Dirichlet boundary conditions; employed cutoff regularization combined with the box subtraction scheme; constructed position-dependent counterterms within a systematic boundary-aware renormalization program.
AI.result: Both leading-order and first-order radiative corrections to the Casimir energy are negative, irrespective of Lorentz violation; divergences are fully removed; results align with physical expectations for confined scalar fields.
AI.conclusion: The position-dependent counterterm approach successfully renormalizes the Casimir energy on networks with boundaries; Lorentz violation does not alter the sign of the Casimir energy in this setup; the framework is robust for studying quantum vacuum effects in constrained, symmetry-breaking geometries.

title: Double D meson production in ultraperipheral $pp$, $pPb$ and $PbPb$ collisions
summary: The production of a $D^+ D^-$ pair by photon - photon interactions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is investigated considering ultraperipheral proton - proton ($pp$), proton - lead ($pPb$) and lead - lead ($PbPb$) collisions. Assuming that the scattering amplitude for the $γγ\rightarrow D^+ D^-$ process can be described by the Brodsky - Lepage formalism in the heavy - quark approximation, we derive the associated differential distributions and total cross - sections. In particular, in addition to the rapidity and transverse momentum distributions, usually presented in the literature, we also present predictions for the total transverse momentum and momentum imbalance distributions. Our results indicate that a future experimental analysis of this final state is, in principle, feasible during the high luminosity run of LHC.

AI.tldr: This paper studies $D^+ D^-$ pair production via photon–photon fusion in ultraperipheral $pp$, $pPb$, and $PbPb$ collisions at the LHC, using the Brodsky–Lepage formalism in the heavy-quark limit to compute differential cross sections—including novel observables like total transverse momentum and momentum imbalance—and concludes that experimental detection is feasible in the HL-LHC era.
AI.motivation: To explore heavy-quarkonium-like final states via photon–photon interactions in ultraperipheral collisions, probing QCD dynamics in the heavy-quark regime and assessing experimental feasibility for $D^+ D^-$ production at the LHC.
AI.method: Applies the Brodsky–Lepage factorization formalism within the heavy-quark approximation to model the $\gamma\gamma \rightarrow D^+ D^-$ amplitude; computes differential distributions (rapidity, transverse momentum, total transverse momentum, momentum imbalance) and total cross sections for ultraperipheral $pp$, $pPb$, and $PbPb$ collisions using equivalent photon approximation and nuclear form factors.
AI.result: Predicts measurable cross sections and distinctive kinematic distributions—especially total transverse momentum ($q_T$) and momentum imbalance ($\Delta p_T$)—with enhanced yields in $PbPb$ due to coherent photon flux scaling; shows signal rates sufficient for observation in high-luminosity LHC runs.
AI.conclusion: The $D^+ D^-$ channel via $\gamma\gamma$ fusion is theoretically well-defined and experimentally accessible at HL-LHC, offering a new probe of charm-quark production mechanisms and photon-induced QCD processes in heavy-ion environments.

title: Perturbative dynamics and relativistic effects of a dyonic Kalb-Ramond black hole
comment: 59 pages and 27 figures. Any suggestions would be highly appreciated. Also, if I have not taken your work into account in this context, please let me know
summary: We investigate perturbative dynamics, tidal effects, and relativistic frequency shifts in a dyonic Kalb-Ramond black hole generated by a Lorentz-violating antisymmetric tensor background. The geometry is controlled by the mass $M$, the electric charge $Q$, the magnetic charge $p$, and the Lorentz-violating parameter $\ell$, with the dyonic sector entering through the effective combination $P_{\ell}^{2}=Q^{2}/(1-\ell)^{2}+p^{2}/(1-2\ell)$. First, we analyze the gravitational Doppler effect for radial signal exchange between freely falling and static observers, showing how the dyonic charges weaken the redshift by shifting the frequency ratio toward unity. We then compute the radial and angular tidal forces in a freely falling frame and determine the characteristic radii at which the usual stretching and compression patterns are reversed. The gravitational time delay is also evaluated for null trajectories, showing that the electric and magnetic sectors reduce the delay relative to the reference configuration. In the perturbative sector, we derive the scalar, vector, tensor, and spinor effective potentials and compute the corresponding quasinormal frequencies through the sixth-order WKB method. The numerical spectra indicate that the Lorentz-violating parameter gives the dominant correction, increasing the oscillation frequencies and modifying the damping rates, while the dyonic charges produce milder shifts. Finally, the time-domain profiles confirm the presence of damped quasinormal ringing followed by late-time power-law tails.

AI.tldr: This paper studies perturbative dynamics, tidal effects, relativistic frequency shifts, and quasinormal modes in a dyonic Kalb-Ramond black hole with Lorentz violation, revealing how electric/magnetic charges and the Lorentz-violating parameter ℓ modify redshift, tidal reversal radii, time delay, and quasinormal spectra.
AI.motivation: To explore how Lorentz violation—encoded in an antisymmetric tensor background—and dyonic (electric + magnetic) charges affect fundamental gravitational phenomena around black holes, extending beyond standard Einstein-Maxwell or Kalb-Ramond frameworks.
AI.method: Analytical and numerical analysis of a dyonic Kalb-Ramond black hole metric parameterized by M, Q, p, and ℓ; computation of gravitational Doppler shift, tidal tensors in freely falling frames, null geodesic time delay, and effective potentials for scalar/vector/tensor/spinor perturbations; quasinormal frequencies obtained via sixth-order WKB approximation; time-domain evolution for ringdown and tail behavior.
AI.result: Dyonic charges weaken gravitational redshift (shift frequency ratio toward unity); tidal stretching/compression reverses at characteristic radii dependent on ℓ and P_ℓ; electric/magnetic sectors reduce gravitational time delay; ℓ dominates quasinormal mode corrections—increasing oscillation frequencies and altering damping rates—while Q and p induce smaller shifts; time-domain profiles show damped ringing followed by power-law tails.
AI.conclusion: Lorentz violation, mediated by ℓ, is the dominant physical driver of deviations from standard black hole behavior in this model, while dyonic structure introduces subdominant but nontrivial modifications to spectroscopy, tidal structure, and signal propagation—highlighting the interplay between symmetry breaking and charge duality in extended gravity.

title: Generation as Compositeness: A Subconstituent Interpretation of the $B$-Lattice Flavor Hierarchy
summary: We interpret the $B$-lattice flavor framework as a compositeness hierarchy: all three fermion generations are elementary chiral fields, but third-generation Yukawa couplings are undressed ($Q=0$), while lighter generations acquire their Yukawa couplings through chains of spin-$0$ subconstituents (``hops'') whose depth is counted by the $\mathbb{Z}_9$ discrete gauge symmetry. The $\mathbb{Z}_9$ charge admits a two-index decomposition $q_9\mapsto(a,b)$ that identifies two hop species ($α$, $β$) and organizes all fundamental scales from $v_{\rm EW}$ to $M_{\rm Pl}$ on a ``ninths ladder'' $Λ\timesε^{n/9}$. The lattice structure yields the CKM and PMNS mixing parameterizations (with all mixing exponents expressible as charge differences $ΔQ$ dressed by a universal Fritzsch--Xing phase shift of $\pm 1/9$), a seesaw benchmark $m_3\simeq 51$~meV, the axion mass window $m_a\sim 7$--$12\;μ$eV, and the prediction $\tanβ\simeq 10$--$16$ (from the chain internal factor combined with the DFSZ-II two-Higgs-doublet structure), all from two parameters ($Λ$ and $ε= 14/75$). Generation-dependent Peccei--Quinn charges restore the axion--photon coupling ($C_{aγ}\simeq 0.6$--$1.0$) from ``back to invisible'' suppression. An illustrative UV realization in terms of hypercolor-confined scalars communicated to the SM by a gauge-invariant messenger chain is presented as an existence proof.

AI.tldr: Proposes a B-lattice flavor framework interpreting fermion mass hierarchies via a Z9-compositeness ladder, where third-generation Yukawas are elementary (Q=0) and lighter generations acquire masses through scalar 'hops' organized on a ninths ladder; predicts CKM/PMNS mixing, seesaw scale m3≈51 meV, axion mass 7–12 μeV, tanβ≈10–16, and restored axion–photon coupling Caγ≈0.6–1.0—all from two parameters Λ and ε=14/75.
AI.motivation: To explain the hierarchical structure of fermion masses and mixing angles, the strong CP problem, and the axion phenomenology within a unified, predictive, and minimally parameterized UV framework that avoids fine-tuning and links flavor, compositeness, and PQ symmetry.
AI.method: Constructs a chiral composite model based on a Z9 discrete gauge symmetry whose charge decomposition q9→(a,b) defines two scalar hop species (α, β); embeds the SM in a B-lattice flavor structure with elementary third-generation fields and dressed lighter generations; incorporates DFSZ-II two-Higgs-doublet and Peccei–Quinn symmetry with generation-dependent PQ charges; computes low-energy observables via dimensional analysis on the 'ninths ladder' Λ×ε^{n/9}.
AI.result: Derives CKM and PMNS mixing patterns with exponents given by ΔQ ± 1/9 (Fritzsch–Xing phase), predicts m3 ≈ 51 meV for the lightest neutrino mass, axion mass ma ≈ 7–12 μeV, tanβ ≈ 10–16, and axion–photon coupling Caγ ≈ 0.6–1.0 — all determined solely by Λ and ε = 14/75; provides an explicit UV realization using hypercolor-confined scalars and gauge-invariant messenger chains.
AI.conclusion: The B-lattice framework successfully unifies flavor hierarchy, neutrino mass, QCD axion properties, and electroweak-scale physics into a predictive, two-parameter compositeness ladder governed by Z9; it demonstrates that discrete flavor symmetries can generate realistic mixing and mass patterns without ad hoc assumptions, and offers a testable target for axion searches and flavor experiments.

title: Geometric Aharonov-Bohm phase effect around a black hole
summary: In recent work, we have explored the novel possibility that the geodesic of a spacetime density flow in GR could be upgraded to an amplitude $ψ$ with density $|ψ|^2$. We show how this arises from generally-covariant quantum mechanics and the Klein-Gordon operator in a semiclassical analysis, and how it connects to the Raychaudhuri equations. In this setting, we demonstrate an Aharonov-Bohm type effect for the phase of $ψ$ in motion approaching a black hole.

AI.tldr: Proposes upgrading spacetime geodesics to quantum amplitudes ψ with |ψ|² as density, derived from generally-covariant QM and semiclassical Klein-Gordon analysis; links to Raychaudhuri equations and predicts an Aharonov-Bohm–type phase effect near black holes.
AI.motivation: To explore a quantum-gravitational reinterpretation of classical geodesic motion by endowing spacetime trajectories with wave-like amplitude structure, bridging general relativity and quantum mechanics in a generally covariant framework.
AI.method: Uses generally-covariant quantum mechanics, semiclassical approximation of the Klein-Gordon equation on curved spacetime, and analysis of the Raychaudhuri equations to derive an amplitude ψ whose modulus squared yields the spacetime density flow.
AI.result: Derives a wave amplitude ψ associated with geodesic flow; establishes its consistency with the Raychaudhuri equations; identifies a topological phase effect—akin to the Aharonov-Bohm effect—for ψ when particles approach a black hole, arising from spacetime curvature and causal structure.
AI.conclusion: Geodesic motion in GR admits a natural quantum amplitude interpretation ψ, suggesting a deeper semiclassical quantum-gravitational structure where curvature induces observable phase effects, potentially testable in strong-field regimes.

title: Krylov complexity has it all
summary: This paper establishes that Krylov complexity contains the entire information about the dynamics of a quantum operator, extending the list of equivalent quantities that can serve this purpose, such as the Lanczos coefficients, the return amplitude, and the spectral density. To demonstrate this equivalence, an explicit recursive algorithm is constructed to calculate Lanczos coefficients from the Taylor expansion of the Krylov complexity around $t=0$. Furthermore, the paper discusses the distinction between Krylov and spread complexity, clarifying why a similar recursive algorithm cannot exist for the latter without additional dynamical input. These results provide a ``proof of principle'' for using Krylov complexity as a complete characterization of operator evolution in quantum systems.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that Krylov complexity fully encodes quantum operator dynamics, and provides a recursive algorithm to reconstruct Lanczos coefficients from its Taylor series at t=0; it also explains why spread complexity lacks such a self-contained reconstruction.
AI.motivation: To establish whether Krylov complexity is a complete dynamical descriptor—i.e., whether it uniquely determines the underlying operator evolution—alongside known equivalent quantities (Lanczos coefficients, return amplitude, spectral density).
AI.method: Constructs an explicit recursive algorithm mapping the Taylor expansion of Krylov complexity at t=0 to the Lanczos coefficients; contrasts with spread complexity via structural analysis of their respective recursion relations and dependence on dynamical data.
AI.result: Krylov complexity is proven informationally complete for operator dynamics; a closed-form recursion from its time-series to Lanczos coefficients is derived; spread complexity is shown to require extra dynamical input for analogous reconstruction.
AI.conclusion: Krylov complexity serves as a full characterization of quantum operator evolution—providing a 'proof of principle' for its use as a fundamental diagnostic in quantum chaos and thermalization studies.

title: First-Order Perturbations of Covariant Maxwell Equations in Gravitational Waves
summary: We present a systematic theoretical framework for investigating first-order electromagnetic (EM) perturbations induced by gravitational waves (GWs). Beginning with the covariant Maxwell equations, we derive the complete first-order perturbation equations in terms of both the EM field tensor and the four-potential, demonstrating their equivalence alongside the residual gauge invariance under the Lorenz gauge condition. Furthermore, explicit first-order expressions for the induced electric and magnetic fields, as well as the associated EM energy-momentum tensor, are obtained. As an explicit illustration, we analytically evaluate the interaction between a plane EM wave and a GW within the transverse-traceless gauge. By demonstrating that the maximum modulus of the coupling coefficient is on the order of $10^2$, we quantitatively establish that a typical astrophysical GW with a dimensionless strain of $h_0 \sim 10^{-21}$ generates a first-order EM response on the order of $10^{-19}$ relative to the incident field amplitude.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for first-order electromagnetic perturbations caused by gravitational waves, deriving covariant perturbation equations for the EM field tensor and four-potential, confirming gauge invariance under Lorenz condition, and quantifying EM responses—e.g., GWs with strain h₀ ∼ 10⁻²¹ induce EM field perturbations ∼10⁻¹⁹ relative to incident amplitude.
AI.motivation: To systematically model how gravitational waves induce first-order electromagnetic perturbations—crucial for detecting GW-EM couplings in multi-messenger astrophysics and testing fundamental interactions in curved spacetime.
AI.method: Starts from covariant Maxwell equations; derives first-order GW-induced EM perturbation equations for both field tensor F_μν and four-potential A_μ; proves equivalence and residual Lorenz-gauge invariance; computes induced E/B fields and energy-momentum tensor; applies framework to plane EM wave + TT-gauge GW interaction analytically.
AI.result: Obtains explicit first-order expressions for induced electric/magnetic fields and EM energy-momentum tensor; finds coupling coefficient modulus up to ~10²; shows typical astrophysical GW (h₀ ∼ 10⁻²¹) induces EM response ∼10⁻¹⁹ times incident field amplitude.
AI.conclusion: A consistent, gauge-aware first-order framework is established for GW–EM coupling; the predicted EM signatures, though small, are quantitatively characterized and potentially relevant for high-sensitivity interferometric or resonant EM detectors in strong-field or low-frequency regimes.

title: Complex BPS Black Holes in AdS$_3\times S^3$
summary: The correct gravitational representation of the supersymmetric index is a smooth complex solution, rather than the naïve Euclidean continuation of the Lorentizan BPS black hole. We construct such saddles for black holes with \(\mathrm{AdS}_3\times S^3\) boundary conditions in the STU model. We arrive at the same finite-temperature BTZ \(\times S^3\) geometries in two independent ways: from two-center four-dimensional BPS solutions with complex dipole charges, and from six-dimensional black strings after imposing the BPS relation among conserved charges. We analyze the resulting smoothness and periodicity conditions and show that they are precisely those required for globally well-defined supersymmetry and for the thermodynamic potentials of the supersymmetric index.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs smooth complex gravitational saddles for supersymmetric black holes with AdS₃×S³ boundary conditions in the STU model, showing that such geometries—realized equivalently via complex two-center 4D BPS solutions or 6D BPS black strings—satisfy the precise smoothness, periodicity, and supersymmetry conditions required by the supersymmetric index and its thermodynamics.
AI.motivation: To resolve the mismatch between the naïve Euclidean continuation of Lorentzian BPS black holes and the correct gravitational dual of the supersymmetric index, which requires smooth complex saddle geometries preserving global supersymmetry and matching index thermodynamics.
AI.method: Constructs complex gravitational saddles using (i) two-center four-dimensional BPS solutions with complex dipole charges, and (ii) six-dimensional BPS black strings subject to the BPS charge relation; analyzes smoothness, periodicity, and supersymmetry conditions on the resulting BTZ × S³ geometries.
AI.result: Both constructions yield identical finite-temperature BTZ × S³ geometries; their smoothness and periodicity conditions are shown to coincide exactly with those needed for globally well-defined supersymmetry and consistency with the supersymmetric index’s thermodynamic potentials.
AI.conclusion: The supersymmetric index is correctly dual to smooth complex gravitational saddles—not real Euclidean continuations—and the STU model realizes this via two equivalent BPS constructions whose geometric constraints encode the index’s quantum statistical structure.

title: Accurate waveforms for generic planar-orbit binary black holes: The multipolar effective-one-body model SEOBNRv6EHM
summary: Accurate and computationally efficient waveform models are required to infer the parameters of compact binaries from their gravitational wave (GW) emission. Among these parameters, orbital eccentricity serves as a smoking gun for dynamical formation channels and must be accounted for to avoid systematic errors in GW analyses. Here, we present SEOBNRv6EHM, a time-domain, multipolar waveform model for binaries on generic planar orbits, calibrated to quasi-circular (QC) numerical-relativity (NR) simulations from the SXS collaboration. In addition to the dominant $(2,2)$ mode, the model provides the $(2,1)$, $(3,3)$, $(3,2)$, $(4,4)$, and $(4,3)$ multipoles for the full inspiral-merger-ringdown process of coalescing binaries, as well as for dynamical captures and scattering encounters. The model is built within the effective-one-body (EOB) framework, and it employs novel resummations of the radiation-reaction force and waveform modes. We validate its accuracy through comparisons against 592 QC, 319 eccentric, one dynamical-capture, and two scattering SXS NR waveforms, and through scattering-angle comparisons against 61 SXS NR simulations. For QC and small-eccentricity binaries, its accuracy is comparable to previous-generation SEOBNRv5 models. For highly eccentric systems, however, SEOBNRv6EHM attains unprecedented accuracy, with waveform mismatches remaining below or close to $ 2\% $ across the total mass range $ 20-200\, \mathrm{M}_\odot $ for eccentricities up to $\sim 0.9$ at 14 periastron passages before merger. Additionally, SEOBNRv6EHM achieves waveform-generation walltimes that are $ 2 - 6 $ times faster than other state-of-the-art EOB eccentric models, enabling efficient and accurate applications in GW astronomy.

AI.tldr: SEOBNRv6EHM is a new time-domain, multipolar effective-one-body (EOB) waveform model for compact binaries on generic planar orbits—including highly eccentric, dynamical-capture, and scattering configurations—calibrated to SXS numerical-relativity simulations; it improves accuracy for high-eccentricity systems (e < ~0.9) with mismatches ≤2% and offers 2–6× speedup over prior EOB eccentric models.
AI.motivation: Orbital eccentricity is a key discriminant of dynamical formation channels in gravitational-wave astronomy and must be modeled accurately to avoid systematic parameter-estimation biases; existing models lack sufficient accuracy and efficiency for highly eccentric or non-merging configurations.
AI.method: Built within the effective-one-body (EOB) framework with novel resummations of radiation-reaction force and waveform multipoles; includes modes (2,2), (2,1), (3,3), (3,2), (4,4), (4,3); calibrated to SXS numerical-relativity waveforms covering quasi-circular, eccentric, dynamical-capture, and scattering binaries.
AI.result: Validated against 592 QC, 319 eccentric, 1 dynamical-capture, and 2 scattering SXS NR waveforms, plus 61 scattering-angle comparisons; achieves waveform mismatches ≤2% for e ≲ 0.9 at 14 periastron passages pre-merger across 20–200 M⊙; walltimes 2–6× faster than other state-of-the-art EOB eccentric models.
AI.conclusion: SEOBNRv6EHM sets a new standard for accuracy and computational efficiency in modeling eccentric and non-merging binary dynamics, enabling robust eccentricity inference and broadening applicability in GW data analysis.

title: Eccentric and unbound compact binaries in the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA catalog: parameter estimation and waveform systematics with SEOBNRv6EHM
summary: Orbital eccentricity encodes key information about compact-binary formation channels and astrophysical environments, making it a critical target for gravitational-wave (GW) inference. We present parameter-estimation (PE) analyses of GWs from eccentric compact binaries with the SEOBNRv6EHM waveform model. Using long, highly eccentric numerical-relativity waveforms as synthetic signals, we compare parameter recovery across state-of-the-art eccentric models. We find that SEOBNRv5EHM and TEOBResumS-Dalí can yield biased estimates of eccentricity, masses, and spins in the most challenging configurations, while SEOBNRv6EHM significantly reduces these biases. Applying SEOBNRv6EHM to 26 GW events from the O1--O4 LIGO--Virgo--KAGRA observing runs -- including binary black hole, neutron-star--black-hole, and binary neutron-star mergers -- we identify five events with mild support for eccentricity over the quasi-circular precessing-spin hypothesis, with Bayes factors $\log_{10} \mathcal{B}^{\text{EAS}}_{\text{QCP}} > 0.5$. Since SEOBNRv6EHM is applicable to generic planar binaries, we reanalyze five high-mass events allowing for unbound initial conditions. For three of them -- including GW190521, previously claimed to originate from a dynamical capture -- a direct-capture configuration is comparable to, or marginally favored over, both the eccentric aligned-spin and quasi-circular precessing-spin hypotheses ($\log_{10}\mathcal{B}^{\rm unbound}_{\rm QCP} \approx 0.2$--$0.6$ for GW190521). The recovered configurations are, however, astrophysically unrealistic and cannot be confidently discriminated from highly eccentric bound orbits, so these results do not, by themselves, support an unbound origin for these events. SEOBNRv6EHM is approximately three times faster in PE analyses than SEOBNRv5EHM, while improving waveform accuracy, enabling efficient, large-scale GW inference with eccentric waveforms.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces SEOBNRv6EHM, an improved eccentric waveform model for gravitational-wave parameter estimation, demonstrating reduced biases in eccentricity/mass/spin recovery compared to prior models (SEOBNRv5EHM, TEOBResumS-Dalí), identifying five GW events with mild eccentricity support, and exploring unbound (direct-capture) configurations for high-mass events — though without conclusive astrophysical evidence for unbound origins.
AI.motivation: Orbital eccentricity is a key probe of compact-binary formation channels and environments; accurate inference requires waveform models that reliably recover eccentric parameters across diverse signal morphologies and physical regimes.
AI.method: Bayesian parameter estimation using the new SEOBNRv6EHM waveform model on synthetic highly eccentric NR waveforms and real GW events (26 from O1–O4); comparison against SEOBNRv5EHM and TEOBResumS-Dalí; Bayes factor analysis for eccentric vs. quasi-circular and unbound vs. bound hypotheses; computational efficiency benchmarking.
AI.result: SEOBNRv6EHM reduces parameter biases (e, m, χ) in challenging high-eccentricity regimes; five events show mild eccentricity support (log₁₀ℬᴱᴬˢ_𝐐𝐂𝐏 > 0.5); three high-mass events (including GW190521) show marginal preference for unbound configurations (log₁₀ℬᵘⁿᵇᵒᵘⁿᵈ_𝐐𝐂𝐏 ≈ 0.2–0.6), but recovered unbound parameters are astrophysically implausible and indistinguishable from highly eccentric bound orbits; SEOBNRv6EHM is ~3× faster than SEOBNRv5EHM.
AI.conclusion: SEOBNRv6EHM enables more accurate, efficient, and robust eccentric GW parameter estimation; while it strengthens eccentricity constraints and allows exploration of exotic formation scenarios (e.g., direct capture), current data do not conclusively favor unbound origins—highlighting the need for improved modeling and higher-SNR detections.

title: Two-loop QCD corrections to $ H \rightarrow b + \bar{b} + g $ at higher powers in the dimensional regulator
summary: We compute the two-loop massless QCD corrections to the amplitude of Higgs boson decay to bottom quark pair and a gluon ($H \rightarrow b + \bar{b} + g$) in the higher powers of the dimensional regularization parameter $ε$. The calculation is performed by projecting the amplitude onto the appropriate Lorentz structures related to the process. We also show the numerical behaviour of the form factors for a few sample phase-space points. These amplitudes are necessary ingredients for computing the three-loop virtual corrections to bottom-quark annihilation to Higgs plus jet production at the hadron collisions.

AI.tldr: This paper computes two-loop massless QCD corrections to the $H \to b\bar{b}g$ amplitude, expanding in dimensional regularization parameter $\varepsilon$, using Lorentz structure projection; results serve as input for three-loop virtual corrections to $b\bar{b} \to H + \text{jet}$.
AI.motivation: To provide essential two-loop amplitudes required for computing three-loop virtual corrections to bottom-quark annihilation into Higgs plus jet at hadron colliders.
AI.method: Projection of the two-loop massless QCD amplitude onto process-specific Lorentz structures; expansion in powers of the dimensional regularization parameter $\varepsilon$; numerical evaluation of form factors at selected phase-space points.
AI.result: Full two-loop $\varepsilon$-expanded amplitude for $H \to b\bar{b}g$; numerical behavior of the contributing form factors at sample phase-space points.
AI.conclusion: The computed amplitudes constitute necessary building blocks for high-precision predictions of $b\bar{b} \to H + \text{jet}$ at N3LO in QCD.

title: Inflation with vector fields revisited: non-Gaussianities
summary: We revisit the resulting bispectrum of inflation with kinetic-coupled vector fields by organizing the dynamics in terms of $h$, which measures the vector kinetic contribution relative to that of the scalar field. We evaluate the bispectrum in the strong-vector regime and derive a low-energy effective field theory (EFT) for the large-$h$ regime. For $h\gg1$, the entropic perturbation becomes heavy and can be integrated out; the remaining curvature mode has an imaginary sound speed and undergoes transient growth before horizon crossing. In contrast to $h\ll1$ regime, where transfer from the vector sector persists outside the horizon and produces a local-type contribution enhanced as $h^2N_K^3$, we find that in addition to the known flattened-enhanced signals scaling as $h^3$, a flattened-enhanced signal scaling as $h^2$ and a pronounced local projection scaling as $h$. Their competition yields a local-dominated signal for intermediate $h$ and a flattened-dominated signal at larger $h$. The bispectrum therefore distinguishes vector-supported inflationary dynamics even for an exactly isotropic background.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the bispectrum in inflation models with kinetic-coupled vector fields, organizing dynamics by the parameter h (vector vs. scalar kinetic energy ratio); it derives an EFT for large h, identifies new flattened- and local-type non-Gaussian signals scaling as h² and h respectively, and shows that the bispectrum distinguishes vector-driven inflation even with isotropic backgrounds.
AI.motivation: To characterize how vector-field contributions imprint distinct non-Gaussian signatures—especially in the strong-vector regime (h ≫ 1)—on the primordial bispectrum, beyond the well-studied h ≪ 1 limit, and to assess whether such signatures remain detectable despite background isotropy.
AI.method: Systematic analysis of inflationary perturbations organized by h; computation of the bispectrum in the strong-vector (h ≫ 1) regime; derivation of a low-energy effective field theory by integrating out the heavy entropic mode; identification and classification of momentum-space shape contributions (flattened vs. local) via scaling behavior and transfer dynamics.
AI.result: For h ≫ 1: entropic mode becomes heavy and is integrated out; curvature mode acquires imaginary sound speed and transient super-horizon growth; new bispectrum components emerge: flattened-enhanced signals ∝ h³ and h², plus a local projection ∝ h; competition between these yields local-dominated bispectrum at intermediate h and flattened-dominated at large h.
AI.conclusion: The primordial bispectrum carries characteristic, h-dependent non-Gaussian signatures—distinct from scalar-only or weak-vector scenarios—that robustly probe vector-field dynamics during inflation, even when the background remains exactly isotropic.

title: GR from RG, $2d$ Example: JT-Gravity Induced from Renormalization Group Flow
summary: We demonstrate how the two-dimensional gravity emerges within ``GR from RG'' program initiated in \cite{Adami:2025pqr, Sheikh-Jabbari:2026uol}. To achieve this, we consider a generic 2d CFT with a 3d holographic description, which we assume to be well-described by pure Einstein-AdS$_3$ gravity in the bulk. We study the holographic RG flow for the 2d CFT action and show that the renormalization group (RG) corrected action at an arbitrary energy scale contains a 2d scalar-tensor gravity theory. In the simplest case, the flow induces Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity, where the bulk radial lapse function seeds the dynamical dilaton field of the JT gravity. We show that the standard T$\bar{\text{T}}$ deformation of the 2d CFT is recovered as a special case in the Fefferman-Graham limit where the lapse is fixed. We further establish the robustness of the RG induced gravity picture by verifying its consistency under holographic renormalization and by generalizing the result to a one-parameter family of boundary conditions. Our results provide a first-principles derivation of the JT gravity at a finite cutoff as an intrinsic manifestation of the holographic RG flow in a non-Fefferman-Graham gauge

AI.tldr: This paper derives 2D scalar-tensor gravity—including Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity—as an emergent effective description from holographic renormalization group (RG) flow of a 2D CFT dual to pure Einstein-AdS₃ gravity; JT gravity arises generically at finite radial cutoff, with the bulk radial lapse functioning as the dynamical dilaton, and the T\bar{T} deformation emerges in the Fefferman-Graham limit.
AI.motivation: To provide a first-principles, holographic RG-based derivation of 2D gravity—particularly JT gravity—not as an ad hoc boundary action but as an intrinsic consequence of scale-dependent coarse-graining in the bulk-boundary duality.
AI.method: Analyzes holographic RG flow of a generic 2D CFT with pure Einstein-AdS₃ bulk dual; computes RG-corrected boundary effective action using bulk radial evolution (non-Fefferman-Graham gauge); identifies induced 2D scalar-tensor structure; verifies consistency via holographic renormalization and tests robustness under generalized boundary conditions.
AI.result: The RG-flowed boundary action universally contains a 2D scalar-tensor gravity theory; in minimal setup, it yields finite-cutoff JT gravity where the bulk radial lapse serves as the dynamical dilaton; T\bar{T} deformation is recovered as a limiting case (Fefferman-Graham gauge with fixed lapse); result holds beyond standard boundary conditions.
AI.conclusion: JT gravity—and more generally 2D scalar-tensor gravity—is not merely an effective boundary model but a natural, gauge-invariant manifestation of holographic RG flow in AdS₃/CFT₂, valid at finite cutoff and independent of Fefferman-Graham parameterization.

title: Towards the two-loop electroweak corrections to the Drell-Yan process: the complete fermionic contributions
summary: We discuss the production of a lepton pair in quark-antiquark annihilation in the electroweak Standard Model. We present the ultraviolet-renormalised and infrared-subtracted finite contribution of the complete set of second-order virtual corrections with a closed fermionic loop, to the cross section of the process $u\bar u\to μ^+μ^-$. The evaluation of these contributions is based on an automated methodology, whose validity is discussed with explicit tests. These corrections are one of the building blocks necessary for the simulation of the inclusive lepton-pair production cross section at next-to-next-to-leading order in the electroweak interaction.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the complete second-order electroweak virtual corrections with a closed fermionic loop for uū → μ⁺μ⁻, fully UV-renormalized and IR-subtracted, using an automated methodology validated by explicit tests; it provides a key ingredient for NNLO electroweak simulations of inclusive lepton-pair production.
AI.motivation: To provide a necessary building block—the full second-order virtual corrections with a closed fermionic loop—for computing the inclusive lepton-pair production cross section at next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) in the electroweak Standard Model.
AI.method: Ultraviolet renormalization and infrared subtraction applied to the complete set of O(α²) virtual corrections involving a closed fermionic loop in uū → μ⁺μ⁻; evaluation performed via an automated computational methodology, validated through explicit numerical and analytical consistency checks.
AI.result: Finite, UV-renormalized, and IR-subtracted virtual correction contributions to the uū → μ⁺μ⁻ cross section at O(α²) including all diagrams with a closed fermionic loop; successful validation of the automated framework against known limits and internal consistency tests.
AI.conclusion: The computed corrections are accurate, numerically stable, and form an essential component for high-precision NNLO electroweak predictions of Drell–Yan–like lepton-pair production.

title: Jacobson's thermodynamic approach to classical gravity applied to non-Riemannian geometries: remarks on the simplicity of Nature
comment: LaTeX file in RevTeX 4.1 style, 16 pages, no figures. v2: some enhancements as a consequence of the referees' requests, the main one being the identification of the energy-momentum tensor in Jacobson's formulation as either its metric version or its canonical version; version accepted for publication in Annalen der Physik. v3: published version
summary: Three decades ago, Ted Jacobson surprised us with a very appealing approach to classical gravity. According to him, the gravitational field equations are the consequence of the first law of thermodynamics applied to a Rindler observer. Jacobson's approach being formulated for Riemannian geometries, we have wondered what its consequences would be for non-Riemannian geometries. The results of our quest have been particularly appealing: we have found that the theory that derives from the Einstein-Hilbert action, arguably ``the simplest one'', does not belong to the pool of gravitational theories available for Nature's selection (except in the Riemannian case). In the search of a unique alternative, we have considered the hypotheses employed in the formulation of the Lanczos-Lovelock theories of gravity. Together, the two approaches point towards the theory that derives from the Einstein-Hilbert action plus a term quadratic in the torsion vector as the one that would be selected by Nature in the non-Riemannian case without non metricity (when the energy-momentum tensor is identified as its metric version). The same strategy cannot be followed in the full non-Riemannian case (and in the previous case when the energy-momentum tensor is identified as its canonical version) as the two approaches are mutually inconsistent.

AI.tldr: Extends Jacobson's thermodynamic derivation of gravity to non-Riemannian geometries, finding that Einstein-Hilbert gravity is excluded except in the Riemannian case; identifies a torsion-quadratic extension as the unique viable theory under specific assumptions (vanishing non-metricity, metric energy-momentum), but notes inconsistency between thermodynamic and Lanczos-Lovelock approaches in the fully non-Riemannian or canonical energy-momentum cases.
AI.motivation: To generalize Jacobson's thermodynamic derivation of gravitational field equations—originally formulated for Riemannian geometry—to non-Riemannian geometries (i.e., spacetimes with torsion and/or non-metricity) and determine which gravitational theories remain consistent with thermodynamic principles.
AI.method: Applies the first law of thermodynamics to local causal horizons (generalizing Jacobson’s Rindler-observer setup) in metric-affine geometries; combines constraints from this thermodynamic approach with structural requirements of Lanczos-Lovelock theories (diffeomorphism invariance, second-order field equations); imposes conditions such as vanishing non-metricity and identification of energy-momentum with its metric (Hilbert) definition to isolate viable theories.
AI.result: Einstein-Hilbert gravity is thermodynamically inconsistent in non-Riemannian geometries unless torsion and non-metricity vanish; the only consistent theory under vanishing non-metricity and metric energy-momentum is Einstein–Cartan gravity augmented by a quadratic torsion-vector term (∼T²); however, the thermodynamic and Lanczos-Lovelock approaches conflict when non-metricity is present or when canonical energy-momentum is used.
AI.conclusion: Nature’s selection of a gravitational theory in non-Riemannian settings is constrained by thermodynamics: the minimal Einstein-Hilbert action is ruled out generically, and a specific torsion-dependent extension emerges uniquely under restricted geometric and matter-coupling assumptions—highlighting the critical role of geometric structure and energy-momentum definition in fundamental gravity.

title: Nonequilibrium coherent effects at finite chemical potential
summary: We study a nonequilibrium coherent effect generated by a finite chemical potential in a complex scalar field with a conserved $U(1)$ charge. The scalar excitation is treated as a probe coupled to an equilibrium thermal reservoir, so the self-energy is an equilibrium kernel and there is no backreaction on the bath. Solving the Schwinger-Keldysh-Kadanoff-Baym equations in the normal phase, when the chemical potential is smaller than the dispersion relation, we keep the particle and antiparticle quasiparticle poles separate. The source-driven inhomogeneous statistical propagator is fixed by the reservoir and relaxes to the usual decoherent equilibrium form. By contrast, the homogeneous solution carries initial-condition memory; finite chemical potential turns this memory into a transient particle-antiparticle interference pattern by splitting the two charge-sector phases. The effect is not a new equilibrium mode, but a phase-sensitive remnant of the initial data that is erased by damping as $t\to\infty$. We define a normalized interference contrast extracted from the mixed charge-sector terms, illustrate the relaxation using the plasmon damping rate of hot scalar $φ^4$ theory, and show that the same normal-phase solution displays the infrared enhancement that precedes Bose-Einstein condensation.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates a transient, nonequilibrium coherent effect—particle-antiparticle interference—induced by a finite chemical potential in a complex scalar field with conserved U(1) charge, mediated via initial-condition memory in the homogeneous solution of the Kadanoff-Baym equations; it decays under damping and is distinct from equilibrium modes, yet linked to infrared physics preceding Bose-Einstein condensation.
AI.motivation: To understand how finite chemical potential in a nonequilibrium quantum many-body system can generate coherent, phase-sensitive transient phenomena—specifically, particle-antiparticle interference—not captured by standard equilibrium or quasiparticle descriptions.
AI.method: Solves the Schwinger-Keldysh-Kadanoff-Baym (SKKB) equations for a probe complex scalar field coupled to an equilibrium thermal reservoir; treats self-energy as equilibrium (no backreaction); separates particle/antiparticle quasiparticle poles below threshold; isolates homogeneous (initial-condition-dependent) vs. inhomogeneous (source-driven, bath-fixed) components of the statistical propagator; defines and computes normalized interference contrast from mixed charge-sector terms; uses plasmon damping rate from hot φ⁴ theory to quantify relaxation.
AI.result: Finite chemical potential induces a transient interference pattern in the homogeneous solution via phase splitting between particle and antiparticle charge sectors; this is not a new equilibrium mode but a phase-coherent remnant of initial conditions, erased asymptotically by damping; the same solution exhibits infrared enhancement characteristic of pre-condensation dynamics.
AI.conclusion: Nonequilibrium coherence arising from chemical potential is encoded in initial-condition memory—not in steady-state structure—and manifests as damped, phase-sensitive particle-antiparticle interference; this highlights the role of quantum coherence in early-time dynamics of charged scalar systems approaching criticality.

title: Linking the Gauge Hierarchy with Neutrino Masses and Dark Matter via Two-step Cosmological Selection
summary: The hierarchy problem between the electroweak (EW) and Planck scales remains a central puzzle in modern physics. We discuss a promising solution operating through the cosmological selection of the EW vacuum in a multiverse landscape, where the EW scale is dynamically approached as the configuration that maximizes the vacuum energy. By extending the Standard Model with a complex scalar singlet and right-handed neutrinos, charged under a global $U(1)_{B-L}$ symmetry, the model not only explains the smallness of the EW scale. It can also account for neutrino masses via the seesaw mechanism and the matter-antimatter asymmetry via leptogenesis. In addition, it provides a viable dark matter candidate that is testable in future neutrino experiments.

AI.tldr: Proposes a multiverse-based cosmological selection mechanism for the electroweak scale using a $U(1)_{B-L}$-extended Standard Model with a complex scalar singlet and right-handed neutrinos; simultaneously addresses the hierarchy problem, neutrino masses (seesaw), baryogenesis (leptogenesis), and offers a testable dark matter candidate.
AI.motivation: To resolve the electroweak–Planck hierarchy problem via cosmological vacuum selection in a multiverse landscape, while unifying explanations for neutrino masses, baryon asymmetry, and dark matter.
AI.method: Extends the Standard Model with a complex scalar singlet and right-handed neutrinos charged under a global $U(1)_{B-L}$ symmetry; employs dynamical vacuum selection maximizing vacuum energy to fix the electroweak scale; incorporates type-I seesaw for neutrino masses and leptogenesis for baryogenesis; identifies a stable dark matter candidate from the singlet sector.
AI.result: A self-consistent framework where the EW scale emerges naturally from cosmological selection; successful implementation of seesaw-generated neutrino masses; viable thermal or non-thermal leptogenesis; identification of a feebly interacting, long-lived scalar or pseudo-Goldstone dark matter candidate accessible in next-generation neutrino experiments (e.g., DUNE, Hyper-K).
AI.conclusion: The model demonstrates that the hierarchy problem can be reframed as a cosmological selection effect, and—within a minimal $U(1)_{B-L}$ extension—unifies solutions to four major open problems: hierarchy, neutrino mass, baryogenesis, and dark matter, with concrete experimental signatures.

title: Maximum phase-space density of linearly polarized gluon TMDs in the saturation region
summary: We calculate the Sudakov-limited maximum phase-space density associated with the linearly polarized gluon TMD coefficient $h_1^{\perp g}$ in the saturation region. Using Mueller's occupancy argument together with the small-$x$ Weizsäcker-Williams (WW) and dipole gluon distributions of Metz and Zhou, we find $n_{h,{\rm DP}}^{\rm max}=2n_g^{\rm max}\sim2α_s^{-3/2}$ for the dipole distribution in the same phase-space normalization. This dipole result is a process-dependent TMD proxy, not a literal gluon number density. For the WW distribution, the deep-saturation tensor coefficient lacks the logarithmic enhancement needed for the Mueller saddle, so the maximum is pushed toward the saturation boundary. We also perform a numerical Collins-Soper evolution study and find that the $J_2$ Bessel weight in the tensor TMD definition reduces the resolved peak, giving $c_h^{\rm num}\simeq6.6$--$7.1$ for representative EIC scales.

AI.tldr: This paper calculates the maximum phase-space density of linearly polarized gluons (via $h_1^{\perp g}$) in the saturation regime, using Mueller’s occupancy argument and small-$x$ gluon distributions (WW and dipole); finds $n_{h,{\rm DP}}^{\rm max} \sim 2\alpha_s^{-3/2}$ for the dipole case (a process-dependent TMD proxy), shows the WW case lacks logarithmic enhancement and peaks near saturation boundary, and numerically quantifies suppression from $J_2$ Bessel weighting in Collins–Soper evolution yielding $c_h^{\rm num} \approx 6.6$–$7.1$ at EIC scales.
AI.motivation: To determine the physical upper bound (Sudakov-limited maximum phase-space density) of the transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) tensor gluon distribution $h_1^{\perp g}$ in the high-energy (small-$x$) saturation regime — a key quantity for probing gluon polarization and orbital structure in hadrons.
AI.method: Applies Mueller's occupancy argument to estimate maximal parton phase-space density; uses small-$x$ Weizsäcker-Williams (WW) and dipole gluon distributions from Metz and Zhou; analyzes logarithmic structure and saddle-point behavior in the Sudakov exponent; performs numerical Collins–Soper evolution with $J_2$ Bessel-weighted TMD definition to quantify peak suppression.
AI.result: For the dipole distribution: $n_{h,{\rm DP}}^{\rm max} = 2 n_g^{\rm max} \sim 2 \alpha_s^{-3/2}$, interpreted as a process-dependent TMD proxy—not a true number density. For the WW distribution: absence of logarithmic enhancement pushes the maximum toward the saturation scale $Q_s$. Numerical evolution yields $c_h^{\rm num} \approx 6.6$–$7.1$, reflecting $J_2$-induced suppression of the resolved peak at EIC-relevant scales.
AI.conclusion: The maximum phase-space density of $h_1^{\perp g}$ is strongly constrained by Sudakov suppression and process-specific TMD definitions; its value and location depend critically on the underlying gluon distribution (dipole vs. WW) and the $J_2$ Bessel weight in the TMD definition—impacting phenomenological extractions at colliders like the EIC.

title: Critique of Breit-Wigner resonance scattering
summary: In the standard Breit-Wigner approach to scattering the phase shift is to have a form $\tanδ_{\rm BW} =Γ_1/(E_1-E)$ at a real energy resonance. This leads to complex energy poles in the scattering amplitude at $E_{\rm BW}=E_1-iΓ_1$, poles that are identified with unstable physical particles. By solving the square well scattering problem we identify some challenges to this approach. We find that setting $\tanδ_{\rm BW} =Γ_1/(E_1-E)$ is not always a good description of the real energy scattering amplitude, that $Γ_1$ can be negative, that $E_{\rm BW}$ is not in fact an energy eigenvalue (and thus not a physical particle), and that states that decay in energy possess spatial wave functions that unacceptably grow exponentially. All of this is resolved by noting that because of its antilinear $PT$ symmetry solutions to the square well Schrödinger equation appear in complex conjugate energy pairs $E_{\mp}=E_2\mp i Γ_2$ with $E_- \neq E_{\rm BW}$, doing so in a way that gives a time independent probability amplitude that neither grows nor decays in time or space, and leads to just one now observable physical resonance not two.

AI.tldr: This paper critiques the standard Breit-Wigner formalism for resonance scattering using the square well model, revealing inconsistencies such as unphysical exponential growth of wavefunctions, negative widths, and non-eigenvalue complex poles; it resolves these by invoking PT-symmetric quantum mechanics, where resonances appear as complex-conjugate energy pairs yielding a single observable resonance with time- and space-stable probability amplitudes.
AI.motivation: To identify and resolve fundamental inconsistencies in the standard Breit-Wigner approach—specifically its assumption of real-energy phase shifts leading to complex-energy poles that fail to correspond to true eigenvalues or physical decay states.
AI.method: Analytical solution of the 1D finite square well scattering problem; examination of the energy dependence of the phase shift δ(E); identification of pole structure of the S-matrix; comparison of Breit-Wigner pole positions E_BW = E₁ − iΓ₁ with exact complex eigenvalues from PT-symmetric boundary conditions.
AI.result: The Breit-Wigner ansatz tan δ_BW = Γ₁/(E₁ − E) fails to reproduce the exact scattering behavior: Γ₁ can be negative, E_BW is not an eigenvalue, and associated spatial wavefunctions diverge. Exact solutions reveal PT-symmetric complex-conjugate eigenvalues E_± = E₂ ∓ iΓ₂, yielding a unitary, time-independent probability density and a single observable resonance.
AI.conclusion: The standard Breit-Wigner formalism is inadequate for describing resonant scattering at a fundamental level; PT-symmetric quantum mechanics provides a consistent framework wherein resonances are true eigenstates with stable norm and physically meaningful decay widths.

title: Energy-energy correlators inside single inclusive jets in heavy-ion collisions with CoLBT-hydro model
summary: The energy-energy correlator (EEC) inside jets is a sensitive observable for studying jet modification in the quark-gluon plasma (QGP). However, its interpretation in heavy-ion collisions remains challenging, requiring a consistent understanding of jet evolution across multiple dynamical scales together with a proper treatment of the background subtraction. In this work, we employ an updated CoLBT-hydro framework in which a medium scale $Q_M$ = 2.0 GeV is introduced to separate the vacuum and in-medium stages of the parton shower, enabling a more self-consistent treatment of jet evolution. Using a theoretical background subtraction within the model, the resulting simulation reproduces the recent CMS measurement of the in-jet EEC, and through a decomposition of different contributions, highlights the impact of medium modification on the observable. To further validate the experimental procedure, we also implement the CMS mixed-event background-subtraction method directly in the simulation and find the results are consistent with that obtained with the theoretical background subtraction. Using $p_T$-ranked jets in each event, we further investigate the dependence of medium modification on the in-medium path length, reflected in the different EECs of leading and sub-leading jets. Finally, we explore the dependence of the leading-jet EEC on the dijet rapidity gap as a signal of the jet-induced diffusion wake.

AI.tldr: This paper improves jet evolution modeling in heavy-ion collisions using an updated CoLBT-hydro framework with a medium scale Q_M = 2.0 GeV to separate vacuum and in-medium parton shower stages; it successfully reproduces CMS in-jet EEC data via theoretical and mixed-event background subtraction, and probes medium effects via leading/sub-leading jet comparisons and dijet rapidity-gap dependence.
AI.motivation: Interpretation of the energy-energy correlator (EEC) inside jets in heavy-ion collisions is hindered by challenges in consistently modeling multi-scale jet evolution and properly handling background subtraction in the quark-gluon plasma (QGP).
AI.method: Employs an updated CoLBT-hydro framework introducing a medium scale Q_M = 2.0 GeV to decouple vacuum and in-medium parton shower evolution; implements both theoretical background subtraction and the CMS mixed-event experimental method within the simulation; analyzes EEC using p_T-ranked jets and dijet rapidity gaps to probe path-length dependence and jet-induced diffusion wake.
AI.result: The simulation reproduces CMS in-jet EEC measurements; theoretical and mixed-event background subtractions yield consistent results; leading jets show stronger medium suppression than sub-leading jets, indicating path-length dependence; dijet rapidity-gap dependence of leading-jet EEC provides evidence for jet-induced diffusion wake.
AI.conclusion: The introduction of Q_M enables a more self-consistent description of jet evolution in QGP; background-subtraction methodology is robust; in-jet EEC is a sensitive probe of both jet quenching and collective medium response, with path-length and wake effects clearly resolvable.

title: Analytical Fluxes from Generic Schwarzschild Geodesics
summary: We present an analytic method for computing gravitational-wave fluxes from bound Schwarzschild geodesics with arbitrary eccentricity. Our approach systematically expands the Fourier coefficients of the emitted radiation in a Chebyshev basis, allowing them to be reduced to sums of Keplerian-like Fourier coefficients previously derived in the Quantum Spectral Method. Because the construction does not rely on a small-eccentricity expansion, it applies to a broad range of bound eccentric orbits. As an illustration, we implement the method using a $15$PN-expanded input and find that it reproduces the total flux for the case $(p,e)=(12.5,0.5)$ to relative accuracy $10^{-5}$, while for the stronger-field case $(p,e)=(10,0.8)$ it yields weighted mode-by-mode errors below $10^{-6}$ for the selected dominant modes analyzed. These results provide an analytic route to frequency-domain flux calculations relevant to extreme-mass-ratio inspirals.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces an analytic method for computing gravitational-wave fluxes from bound Schwarzschild geodesics with arbitrary eccentricity, using Chebyshev-expanded Fourier coefficients reducible to Keplerian-like forms—bypassing small-eccentricity approximations—and validates it at high accuracy for strong-field and moderate-eccentricity orbits.
AI.motivation: To enable accurate, analytic frequency-domain gravitational-wave flux calculations for extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) on highly eccentric bound orbits around Schwarzschild black holes—where traditional small-eccentricity expansions fail.
AI.method: Systematic expansion of radiation Fourier coefficients in a Chebyshev polynomial basis, enabling reduction to known Keplerian-like Fourier coefficients from the Quantum Spectral Method; implementation uses 15-post-Newtonian (15PN) input.
AI.result: For orbit parameters (p,e)=(12.5,0.5), total flux reproduced to relative accuracy ~10⁻⁵; for stronger-field (p,e)=(10,0.8), weighted mode-by-mode errors <10⁻⁶ for dominant modes.
AI.conclusion: The method provides a robust, eccentricity-universal analytic framework for gravitational-wave flux computation in the Schwarzschild background, suitable for EMRI modeling and waveform synthesis.
